skills.learned: On the job; an IPC/WHMA-A-620 course ending in the Certified IPC Specialist credential is the recognized training.

skills.name: Wire Crimping and Termination
skills.what: Stripping wire and crimping contacts, terminals and splices that hold and conduct. A person who has it picks the tool and die for the contact and wire size, inspects each crimp and proves the setup with a pull test.
skills.learned: On the job; IPC/WHMA-A-620 courses teach and test it.

skills.name: Wire Bundle Lacing and Clamping
skills.what: Tying wire bundles with lacing cord or straps and supporting them with clamps at the right spacing. A person who has it leaves no chafe points, keeps bend radius and separates bundles as the drawing requires.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools and on the job in aerospace wiring.

skills.name: RF and Coaxial Cable Assembly
skills.what: Building coaxial cables: stripping to exact dimensions, fitting crimp or solder connectors and testing the result. A person who has it keeps the cable's geometry intact so signal loss and reflections stay within limits.
skills.learned: On the job in avionics, radar and telecom work.
tools: Crimp and solder connectors such as SMA, TNC and N

skills.name: Connector Assembly
skills.what: Assembling multi-pin connectors: crimping contacts, inserting and extracting them, fitting backshells and strain relief. A person who has it reads the pin-out, seats every contact and checks retention.
skills.learned: On the job in harness, avionics and spacecraft work; IPC/WHMA-A-620 courses cover it.
tools: Circular and rectangular connectors such as MIL-DTL-38999 and D-sub

skills.name: Fiber Optic Termination
skills.what: Fitting connectors to optical fiber or splicing it, then cleaning, inspecting and testing the link. A person who has it cleaves and polishes or fusion-splices, inspects the end face and measures loss.
skills.learned: On the job; short courses from training providers and equipment makers.

skills.name: Electrical Bonding and Grounding
skills.what: Making low-resistance electrical paths between structure, equipment and cable shields so static, lightning and interference have a path to ground. A person who has it prepares the surface, installs the strap or jumper and measures the resistance.
skills.learned: Aviation maintenance schools and on the job in aircraft and spacecraft wiring.

skills.name: Power Electronics Assembly
skills.what: Building inverters, converters and chargers: mounting power modules, capacitors, busbars and control boards in a housing. A person who has it controls torque on electrical joints, creepage and clearance, and thermal interface coverage.
skills.learned: On the job in a power electronics plant.

skills.name: Power Module Assembly
skills.what: Building the power semiconductor modules at the heart of an inverter: die on a substrate, wire or clip bonds, terminals, gel and housing. A person who has it runs the attach, bond and encapsulation steps and reads the inspection results.
skills.learned: On the job at a power module plant.

skills.name: Silver Sintering Die Attach
skills.what: Attaching power dies with a silver paste or film that is pressed and heated into a solid joint able to run hotter than solder. A person who has it controls print or placement, drying and the pressure and temperature of the sinter press.
skills.learned: On the job at a power module plant.

skills.name: Thermal Interface Material Application
skills.what: Applying paste, gap filler or pads between a heat source and its heat sink. A person who has it lays down the right pattern and amount so the gap is filled without voids or squeeze-out.
skills.learned: On the job in electronics, battery and power electronics assembly.
tools: Thermal greases, gap fillers and pads

skills.name: Heat Sink Installation
skills.what: Mounting heat sinks and cold plates on processors and power devices. A person who has it applies the interface material, seats the sink flat and tightens in sequence to even pressure.
skills.learned: On the job in server and power electronics assembly.

skills.name: Cold Plate and Coolant Loop Assembly
skills.what: Assembling the liquid cooling of power electronics: cold plates, hoses, fittings and seals. A person who has it keeps sealing surfaces clean, makes up connections and leak-tests the loop.
skills.learned: On the job in a power electronics plant.

skills.name: Server Component Installation
skills.what: Installing processors, memory, drives, cards and power supplies in a server chassis to a build sheet. A person who has it handles parts under ESD control, seats each fully and records serial numbers.
skills.learned: On the job at a server plant; CompTIA A+ covers the hardware basics.

skills.name: Server Rack Integration
skills.what: Mounting servers, switches and power distribution in a rack and wiring it to a rack elevation drawing. A person who has it installs rails and heavy units safely and labels every unit and cable.
skills.learned: On the job at a server integration plant.

skills.name: Rack Cable Routing and Dressing
skills.what: Routing power and network cables in a rack so each reaches its port with the right length, bend radius and label. A person who has it dresses bundles so airflow and service access stay clear.
skills.learned: On the job at a server integration plant.

skills.name: BIOS and BMC Configuration
skills.what: Setting a server's firmware to the customer's build: BIOS options, boot order, management controller network and credentials, firmware levels. A person who has it applies settings by script or by hand and verifies them.
skills.learned: On the job at a server plant.

skills.name: RAID Configuration
skills.what: Building drive arrays on a server's storage controller to the ordered level and layout. A person who has it creates and initializes the array and confirms every drive is healthy.
skills.learned: On the job at a server plant; covered in server administration courses.

skills.name: Operating System Imaging
skills.what: Loading an operating system image and drivers onto new computers over the network and confirming each unit boots and reports correctly. A person who has it runs the imaging station and clears units that fail.
skills.learned: On the job at a computer or server plant.

skills.name: Device Battery Installation
skills.what: Fitting a lithium battery into a phone or laptop: placing it on its adhesive, routing and connecting the flex. A person who has it never bends, presses or punctures the cell and knows what to do if one is damaged.
skills.learned: On the job at a device assembly plant.

skills.name: Camera Module Assembly
skills.what: Placing a camera module in a device, connecting its flex and fixing it so it stays aligned. A person who has it keeps the lens and sensor free of dust and fingerprints and checks the image after assembly.
skills.learned: On the job at a device assembly plant.

skills.name: Display Module Assembly
skills.what: Bonding and connecting a display to a device housing. A person who has it aligns the panel, applies adhesive or gasket evenly, presses it to the set force and checks for dust, light leak and dead pixels.
skills.learned: On the job at a device assembly plant.

skills.name: Device Sensor Calibration
skills.what: Running the calibration stations that teach each finished device its own touch panel, cameras and motion sensors. A person who has it loads the unit, runs the routine and reads a failure well enough to send it to the right repair.
skills.learned: On the job at a device assembly plant.

skills.name: Device Enclosure Sealing
skills.what: Applying the gaskets and adhesives that keep water and dust out of a device and proving the seal. A person who has it places seals without gaps or twists and runs the leak test.
skills.learned: On the job at a device assembly plant.

skills.name: Phased Array Antenna Assembly
skills.what: Building flat-panel antennas made of many small radiating elements and their circuit boards. A person who has it bonds and fastens the layers, connects them and supports the radio-frequency test that follows.
skills.learned: On the job at an antenna plant.

skills.name: Laser Communication Terminal Assembly
skills.what: Building the optical terminals satellites use to send data by laser: mounting optics, lasers and pointing mechanisms and aligning them. A person who has it works clean and aligns to very small angles.
skills.learned: On the job at a satellite plant, usually from an optics or precision assembly background.

skills.name: Box Build Assembly
skills.what: Building a finished electronic unit in its enclosure: mounting boards, power supplies, fans and connectors, routing and securing cables, fitting covers and labels. A person who has it works from the assembly drawing and bill of material, torques and stakes hardware and leaves wiring that will survive vibration.
skills.learned: On the job as an electronics assembler; IPC-A-610 and IPC/WHMA-A-620 courses cover the workmanship.
tools: Assembly drawings and bills of material

skills.name: Composite Layup
skills.what: Laying plies of carbon, glass or aramid fabric onto a tool in the order and fiber direction the ply table calls for. A person who has it works the material into contours without bridging or wrinkles, keeps it clean and tracks its out-time.
skills.learned: Composite technician programs at community colleges and on the job. The American Composites Manufacturers Association's Certified Composites Technician covers it.

skills.name: Unidirectional Tape Layup
skills.what: Laying unidirectional prepreg tape, whose strength runs one way only, so that each ply's angle is right and edges butt without gaps or overlaps beyond the limit. A person who has it controls splices and steers tape on contours.
skills.learned: On the job after general layup experience.

skills.name: Ply Cutting and Kitting
skills.what: Cutting plies to shape and fiber angle, by knife and template or on a CNC cutter, and kitting them in layup order. A person who has it nests to save material and labels each ply with its number and direction.
skills.learned: On the job in a composites shop.

skills.name: Layup Tool Preparation
skills.what: Getting a layup tool ready: cleaning it, checking the surface and vacuum integrity, and applying release agent in the right number of coats. A person who has it prevents a part sticking to, or being marked by, its tool.
skills.learned: On the job in a composites shop.

skills.name: Debulking
skills.what: Compacting plies under vacuum every few layers to remove trapped air and bulk before cure. A person who has it knows how often and how long the specification requires and bags a temporary debulk quickly.
skills.learned: Learned with layup, on the job.

skills.name: Honeycomb Core Installation
skills.what: Fitting honeycomb or foam core into a sandwich panel: trimming it to shape, splicing sections, potting where fasteners will go and bonding it without crushing. A person who has it keeps ribbon direction right and the core dry and clean.
skills.learned: On the job in a composites shop.

skills.name: Vacuum Bagging
skills.what: Sealing a layup under a vacuum bag for cure: release film, bleeder, breather, bag film, sealant tape and ports in the right order. A person who has it pleats the bag over contours and passes a leak check.
skills.learned: Composite technician programs and on the job; covered by the Certified Composites Technician credential.

skills.name: Thermocouple Placement
skills.what: Placing temperature sensors on a part and tool so the cure is controlled from its hottest and coldest points. A person who has it follows the survey for where the leading and lagging thermocouples go and checks each one before the door closes.
skills.learned: On the job in a composites shop.

skills.name: Autoclave Operation
skills.what: Loading, running and unloading an autoclave that cures composites under heat and pressure. A person who has it connects vacuum and thermocouples, verifies the recipe, watches the run and responds to a lost bag or sensor.
skills.learned: On the job, starting as a loader; autoclave makers train operators on the controls.

skills.name: Cure Cycle Programming
skills.what: Building the heat-up, hold, pressure and cool-down recipe an autoclave or oven follows, from the material specification and the load. A person who has it sets ramp rates and holds so every part in the load meets its cure.
skills.learned: On the job, moving up from autoclave operator; process engineering training.

skills.name: Cure Cycle Monitoring
skills.what: Watching temperature, pressure and vacuum through a cure and reviewing the record afterwards against the specification. A person who has it catches a lagging thermocouple or a leaking bag in time and knows what makes a cure discrepant.
skills.learned: On the job in a composites shop.

skills.name: Cure Exotherm Control
skills.what: Keeping thick laminates and large resin masses from overheating as the resin's own reaction releases heat. A person who has it slows ramps, adds dwells and watches the part thermocouples for a runaway.
skills.learned: On the job, as a senior cure operator or process engineer.

skills.name: Out-of-Autoclave Curing
skills.what: Curing composites under vacuum bag pressure alone in an oven or with heat blankets. A person who has it gets air out of the laminate before the resin flows, because there is no autoclave pressure to close voids.
skills.learned: On the job in a composites shop.

skills.name: Resin Infusion
skills.what: Pulling liquid resin through dry fiber under vacuum, or injecting it into a closed mold. A person who has it lays out feed lines and flow media, checks the bag for leaks, mixes and degasses resin and watches the flow front until the part is filled.
skills.learned: Composite technician programs and on the job; covered by the Certified Composites Technician credential.

skills.name: Composite Trimming and Drilling
skills.what: Cutting cured composite to its edge line and drilling it without delamination, fiber breakout or heat damage. A person who has it uses the right cutter and speed, backs up the exit side and controls dust.
skills.learned: On the job in a composites shop or aerostructures plant.

skills.name: Adhesive Surface Preparation
skills.what: Preparing a surface so adhesive bonds to it: solvent cleaning, abrading or grit blasting, peel ply removal, or anodizing and priming metal. A person who has it proves cleanliness with a water break test and bonds within the allowed time.
skills.learned: On the job in bonding shops.

skills.name: Film Adhesive Application
skills.what: Laying film adhesive on a bond surface. A person who has it handles the film cold, cuts it to the pattern, removes every backing and avoids trapped air and overlaps beyond the limit.
skills.learned: On the job in a bonding shop.

skills.name: Paste Adhesive Application
skills.what: Mixing two-part paste adhesive to ratio and applying it at the right thickness. A person who has it works within pot life, controls bondline thickness and cleans up squeeze-out.
skills.learned: On the job in a bonding shop.
tools: Glass beads or scrim for bondline control

skills.name: Secondary Bonding
skills.what: Joining two already-cured composite parts with adhesive. A person who has it fits the parts dry first, prepares both surfaces, applies adhesive, holds them in a fixture under pressure and cures.
skills.learned: On the job in a bonding shop.

skills.name: Co-Cure and Co-Bond Processing
skills.what: Joining composite details in the cure itself: uncured plies cured together, or uncured plies cured against an already-cured part with adhesive between. A person who has it locates the details on the tool and keeps them in place through bagging and cure.
skills.learned: On the job, after layup and bonding experience.

skills.name: Laminate Layup Inspection
skills.what: Checking a layup as it is built and after cure: ply count and direction, where plies end, wrinkles, bridging, foreign material, and dry or resin-rich areas. A person who has it buys off each ply against the ply table.
skills.learned: On the job as a senior layup technician or inspector.

skills.name: Composite Damage Assessment
skills.what: Finding the extent of damage in composite structure and deciding, from the repair manual, whether it is allowable, repairable or beyond limits. A person who has it maps the damage by visual, tap and ultrasonic inspection.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training plus composite repair courses; on the job.

skills.name: Structural Repair Manual Use
skills.what: Finding and following the approved repair for a structure in the manufacturer's structural repair manual. A person who has it identifies the part and zone, reads the allowable damage limits and picks the right repair scheme.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training; on the job.

skills.name: Composite Drying Before Repair
skills.what: Driving absorbed moisture out of composite structure before a heated repair, so steam does not blister the laminate or weaken the bond. A person who has it applies low heat under vacuum for the specified time and confirms the part is dry.
skills.learned: Composite repair courses and on the job.

skills.name: Scarf and Step Repair
skills.what: Repairing a damaged laminate by sanding the surrounding plies to a shallow taper or a series of steps and laying in matching replacement plies. A person who has it holds the taper ratio, matches ply direction and cures the patch with a hot bonder.
skills.learned: Composite repair courses for aircraft mechanics; on the job under an experienced repair technician.

skills.name: Bolted Composite Repair
skills.what: Repairing composite structure with a fastened metal or composite doubler. A person who has it lays out the fastener pattern, drills composite without delamination and installs fasteners wet with sealant.
skills.learned: FAA Airframe and Powerplant training plus composite repair courses.

skills.name: Automated Fiber Placement
skills.what: Running the machine that lays narrow strips of prepreg tape onto a tool under program control. A person who has it loads and threads spools, watches each course for gaps, laps, twists and missing tows, repairs them by hand and inspects every ply before the next is laid.
skills.learned: On the job at an aerostructures or rocket plant, usually after hand layup; machine makers' operator courses.
tools: Fiber placement and tape laying machines
Laser projection and ply inspection systems

skills.name: Filament Winding
skills.what: Winding resin-wetted fiber onto a rotating mandrel or liner to make pressure vessels, motor cases and tubes. A person who has it sets up the creel and tension, watches the band pattern and resin content as it winds and prepares the part for cure.
skills.learned: On the job at a pressure vessel or rocket motor plant.

skills.name: Quench and Temper Hardening
skills.what: Hardening steel by heating it above its critical temperature, quenching it, then tempering to the hardness wanted. A person who has it loads to limit distortion, holds quench delay and verifies hardness.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat shop; metallurgy courses at community colleges.

skills.name: Carburizing
skills.what: Adding carbon to the surface of low-carbon steel in a furnace atmosphere so that, once quenched, it has a hard case over a tough core. A person who has it controls carbon potential, time and temperature and checks case depth.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat shop.
tools: Oxygen probes and dew point analyzers

skills.name: Nitriding
skills.what: Hardening a steel surface with nitrogen at a temperature low enough to avoid distortion. A person who has it prepares and masks parts, runs the gas or plasma cycle and checks case depth and white layer.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat shop.

skills.name: Annealing and Normalizing
skills.what: Softening metal or refining its grain by heating and controlled cooling, so it can be formed or machined. A person who has it picks the cycle for the alloy and cools at the rate it needs.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat shop; metallurgy courses.

skills.name: Solution Heat Treatment
skills.what: Heating aluminum, titanium or nickel alloys to dissolve their hardening elements, then quenching fast enough to keep them dissolved. A person who has it holds soak time and the maximum quench delay.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat shop.

skills.name: Precipitation Hardening
skills.what: Aging a solution-treated alloy at a controlled temperature and time to bring it to its specified temper, such as T6. A person who has it loads for even heating and verifies the result by hardness and conductivity.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat shop.

skills.name: Stress Relieving
skills.what: Heating a welded, machined or formed part below its transformation temperature and cooling it slowly to remove locked-in stress. A person who has it supports the part so it does not sag and follows the specified cycle.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat or fabrication shop.

skills.name: Vacuum Heat Treatment
skills.what: Heat treating in a vacuum furnace so parts come out clean and bright. A person who has it loads fixtures, sets vacuum level and partial pressure, runs gas quench and leak-checks the furnace.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat shop; furnace makers' training.

skills.name: Aluminum Casting Heat Treatment
skills.what: Bringing aluminum castings to temper, such as T5, T6 or T7, without distorting thin sections. A person who has it racks castings for support and airflow and controls quench.
skills.learned: On the job at a casting plant.

skills.name: Pyrometry
skills.what: Proving that a furnace's temperature measurement is right, as AMS 2750 requires: sensor selection and replacement, instrument calibration and system accuracy tests. A person who has it runs the tests on schedule and keeps the records an audit will ask for.
skills.learned: On the job in a heat treat shop that holds aerospace or automotive approvals; pyrometry courses from industry trainers.
tools: Calibrated test thermocouples and field test instruments

skills.name: Temperature Uniformity Survey
skills.what: Mapping the temperature across a furnace's or autoclave's working zone with a rack of test thermocouples, to show every point stays within the tolerance of its class. A person who has it sets up the survey, runs it and reports it to AMS 2750.
skills.learned: On the job in heat treat and composites; pyrometry courses.

skills.name: Rockwell Hardness Testing
skills.what: Measuring hardness by the depth an indenter sinks under load. A person who has it picks the scale for the material, prepares and supports the part, verifies the tester on test blocks each day and reports a valid reading.
skills.learned: Machining, metallurgy and quality programs; on the job. The method is ASTM E18.

skills.name: Brinell Hardness Testing
skills.what: Measuring the hardness of castings and forgings by pressing a ball into the surface and measuring the dent. A person who has it prepares a flat spot, applies the load for the set time and reads the diameter with a scope.
skills.learned: On the job in foundries, forges and heat treat shops. The method is ASTM E10.

skills.name: Anodizing
skills.what: Growing a protective oxide coating on aluminum in an acid bath under current. A person who has it racks parts for good contact, runs the clean, etch, anodize, dye and seal steps and checks coating thickness.
skills.learned: On the job in a finishing shop. Aerospace work is done to MIL-A-8625 (now MIL-PRF-8625), which defines the coating types.

skills.name: Hard Anodizing
skills.what: Building a thick, wear-resistant oxide coating on aluminum in a chilled bath at higher voltage (MIL-A-8625 Type III). A person who has it allows for the growth in size, prevents burning and masks surfaces that must stay bare.
skills.learned: On the job in a finishing shop after general anodizing experience.

skills.name: Chemical Conversion Coating
skills.what: Treating aluminum with a chemical film that resists corrosion, holds paint and still conducts. A person who has it cleans and deoxidizes the part, controls immersion time and handles the fresh coating gently.
skills.learned: On the job in a finishing shop. The coating is specified by MIL-DTL-5541.
tools: Brush and pen applicators for touch-up

skills.name: Passivation of Stainless Steel
skills.what: Removing free iron from stainless steel in nitric or citric acid so its protective oxide forms fully. A person who has it picks the bath for the grade, controls time and temperature and tests the result.
skills.learned: On the job in a finishing shop. The process is specified by ASTM A967 and AMS 2700.
tools: Copper sulfate and water immersion test kits

skills.name: Electroplating
skills.what: Depositing a metal coating from a solution with current, on racks or in barrels. A person who has it cleans and activates the surface, sets current for the area being plated, controls the bath and bakes high-strength steel afterwards to prevent hydrogen embrittlement.
skills.learned: On the job in a plating shop. The National Association for Surface Finishing teaches a Certified Electroplater-Finisher course.

skills.name: Electroless Nickel Plating
skills.what: Plating a uniform nickel-phosphorus coating by chemical reaction, without current, so recesses and bores are covered evenly. A person who has it holds bath temperature, pH and chemistry and controls thickness by time.
skills.learned: On the job in a plating shop.

skills.name: Hard Chrome Plating
skills.what: Plating thick, hard chromium on wear surfaces such as hydraulic rods, usually followed by grinding to size. A person who has it masks the part, builds conforming anodes for even thickness and bakes for embrittlement relief.
skills.learned: On the job in a plating shop.
tools: Chromic acid tanks with fume control

skills.name: Electropolishing
skills.what: Smoothing and brightening stainless steel by dissolving a thin surface layer in an electrolytic bath. A person who has it racks for even current, sets time and current density and checks finish.
skills.learned: On the job in a finishing shop.

skills.name: Phosphate Pretreatment
skills.what: Running the cleaning and conversion stages that prepare a car body or metal part for paint. A person who has it keeps each stage's temperature, concentration and spray pressures in range by titration and adjustment.
skills.learned: On the job in a paint shop; chemical suppliers train operators.

skills.name: E-Coat Operation
skills.what: Running an electrocoat tank, where a charged body is dipped and primer deposits evenly over every surface, inside and out. A person who has it holds bath solids, pH, conductivity and voltage, keeps the rinses clean and checks film build after bake.
skills.learned: On the job in a paint shop; paint suppliers train operators.

skills.name: Seam Sealer Application
skills.what: Applying sealer to body seams and underbody coating before paint, by hand gun, brush or robot. A person who has it covers each seam fully without skips and tools the bead so it does not show.
skills.learned: On the job in an automotive paint shop.

skills.name: Spray Gun Painting
skills.what: Applying primer, color and clear coat with a spray gun. A person who has it mixes and thins to viscosity, sets fluid, fan and air pressure and lays even, wet coats without runs, dry spray or missed areas.
skills.learned: Auto body and industrial coatings programs; on the job.

skills.name: Robotic Paint Application
skills.what: Running the robots and rotary bell atomizers that paint car bodies. A person who has it adjusts flow, bell speed, shaping air and voltage by zone, keeps applicators clean and corrects film build and appearance from measurements.
skills.learned: On the job in an automotive paint shop; robot and applicator makers' training.

skills.name: Paint Masking
skills.what: Covering what must not be painted and leaving a clean edge. A person who has it picks tape and plugs for the paint and bake temperature and removes masking at the right time.
skills.learned: On the job in a paint shop.

skills.name: Coating Removal and Surface Preparation
skills.what: Taking a surface back to clean metal or sound substrate before coating, by abrasive blasting, sanding or chemical stripping. A person who has it reaches the cleanliness and surface profile the coating needs without damaging the part.
skills.learned: On the job; industrial coatings programs. The Association for Materials Protection and Performance publishes the surface preparation standards.

skills.name: Color Matching
skills.what: Judging and adjusting color so a part matches its standard under more than one light. A person who has it reads spectrophotometer values, compares against master panels and tints or adjusts application to correct a shift.
skills.learned: On the job in a paint shop or paint lab.

skills.name: Paint Defect Identification
skills.what: Recognizing paint defects and what causes them: dirt, craters, runs and sags, orange peel, solvent pop, mottle and thin film. A person who has it marks each defect, classes it and feeds the pattern back to the process.
skills.learned: On the job in a paint shop.

skills.name: Paint Defect Repair
skills.what: Removing a paint defect from a finished surface by sanding and polishing, or by spot repair when it is too deep. A person who has it takes off no more clear coat than needed and leaves no haze or swirl.
skills.learned: On the job in a paint shop; auto body programs.

skills.name: Coating Thickness Measurement
skills.what: Measuring wet and dry coating thickness: paint, powder, anodize and plating. A person who has it verifies the gauge on shims over the same base metal, takes readings in the pattern the specification calls for and knows the acceptable range for each coat.
skills.learned: On the job in a paint or finishing shop; coating inspector courses.
tools: Magnetic and eddy current dry film gauges

skills.name: Paint Appearance Measurement
skills.what: Measuring how a painted surface looks: gloss, orange peel and distinctness of image. A person who has it takes readings at set locations and ties a change to film build, flow or bake.
skills.learned: On the job in an automotive paint shop.

skills.name: Coating Adhesion Testing
skills.what: Proving a coating is bonded to its surface by cross-hatch tape test or pull-off test. A person who has it makes the cuts or bonds the dolly correctly and rates the result against the standard.
skills.learned: On the job in paint and coating work. The cross-hatch tape test is ASTM D3359.

skills.name: Low-Observable Coating Application
skills.what: Applying radar-absorbing coatings and materials to aircraft surfaces. A person who has it controls thickness closely, since performance depends on it, and treats gaps, edges and fasteners as the specification requires.
skills.learned: On the job at a military aircraft plant, with a security clearance, after industrial painting experience.

skills.name: Shot Peening
skills.what: Bombarding a metal surface with shot under control, to leave a compressed layer that resists fatigue cracking. A person who has it masks the part, sets the machine, proves intensity with Almen strips and a saturation curve and verifies coverage.
skills.learned: On the job in a processing shop; the industry's shot peening workshops certify operators at three levels. Aerospace work is done to AMS 2430 and audited under Nadcap.
tools: Cast steel, cut wire, glass and ceramic shot

skills.name: Thermal Spray Coating
skills.what: Spraying molten or softened metal, carbide or ceramic onto a part to build a wear, thermal or corrosion coating, by plasma, high-velocity oxy-fuel or wire arc. A person who has it grit-blasts and masks the part, sets gun parameters and standoff, controls part temperature and sprays test coupons for thickness, bond and structure.
skills.learned: On the job in a coating shop; gun makers' courses. Aerospace work is audited under Nadcap.
tools: Plasma, HVOF and twin-wire arc spray guns

skills.name: Powder Coating
skills.what: Applying dry powder paint with an electrostatic gun and curing it in an oven. A person who has it hangs and grounds parts, sets voltage and powder flow, coats recesses without heavy edges and checks cure and film thickness.
skills.learned: On the job in a finishing shop; the Powder Coating Institute certifies and trains.

skills.name: Positive Material Identification
skills.what: Confirming what alloy a part or bar is, with a handheld X-ray fluorescence analyzer or a spark spectrometer. A person who has it prepares the surface, takes the reading, compares it with the grade's limits and knows which elements the instrument cannot see.
skills.learned: Instrument makers' courses and on the job; X-ray analyzers need radiation safety training.

skills.name: Wafer Handling
skills.what: Moving wafers between carriers and tools without touching, scratching or contaminating them. A person who has it loads pods on a tool, uses a vacuum wand only when allowed and knows what to do with a dropped or broken wafer.
skills.learned: Taught in the first days at a fab and checked before working alone; semiconductor technician programs practice it.

skills.name: Photolithography
skills.what: Printing a circuit pattern onto a wafer: coat with photoresist, expose through a mask on a scanner, develop. A person who has it runs lots through the litho cell, checks the tool's focus and dose monitors and sends wafers on for measurement.
skills.learned: On the job through tool certification; semiconductor manufacturing programs at community colleges teach the process.

skills.name: Photoresist Coating
skills.what: Spinning a uniform film of photoresist onto a wafer on a track: prime, dispense, spin, edge bead removal and soft bake. A person who has it keeps thickness on target and finds the cause of streaks, comets and bubbles.
skills.learned: On the job in a litho area.

skills.name: Photoresist Developing
skills.what: Baking an exposed wafer and washing away the resist that should not remain. A person who has it holds post-exposure bake temperature and develop time, which set the printed line width, and recognizes residue and pattern collapse.
skills.learned: On the job in a litho area.

skills.name: Photoresist Stripping
skills.what: Removing photoresist once it has done its job, by oxygen plasma or wet chemistry, without attacking the layers beneath. A person who has it picks the method for an implanted or etched resist and checks for residue.
skills.learned: On the job in etch or wet process areas.

skills.name: Immersion Lithography
skills.what: Exposing wafers on a 193 nm scanner that keeps a film of water between lens and wafer to print finer features. A person who has it watches for immersion-specific defects such as water marks and bubbles and keeps the wafer edge and topcoat in control.
skills.learned: On the job as an experienced litho technician or engineer; scanner makers' training.

skills.name: EUV Lithography
skills.what: Exposing wafers with 13.5 nm extreme ultraviolet light, in vacuum, from reflective masks. A person who has it monitors dose, focus and source power, handles EUV reticles and pellicles and tracks the random defects that EUV is prone to.
skills.learned: On the job at a leading-edge fab; ASML trains customers' engineers and its own field service engineers.

skills.name: Focus-Exposure Matrix Analysis
skills.what: Exposing a wafer with stepped focus and dose, measuring the result and finding the settings that give the widest process window. A person who has it reads Bossung curves and sets the scanner's best focus and dose.
skills.learned: On the job as a litho process technician or engineer.

skills.name: Optical Proximity Correction
skills.what: Adjusting mask shapes in software so that what prints on the wafer matches the design despite diffraction. A person who has it builds and calibrates the model from wafer measurements and verifies the corrected layout.
skills.learned: Engineering degree and on-the-job training in a fab or mask data group.

skills.name: Critical Dimension Measurement
skills.what: Measuring the width of the smallest printed and etched features and comparing it with target. A person who has it picks the sites, runs the measurement and reads the trend across a wafer and lot.
skills.learned: On the job in a metrology area.

skills.name: CD-SEM Operation
skills.what: Running the scanning electron microscope that measures line widths in production. A person who has it writes and edits measurement recipes, sets pattern recognition and focus and avoids charging and resist shrink that distort the reading.
skills.learned: On the job; tool makers' training.

skills.name: Overlay Measurement
skills.what: Measuring how well one patterned layer lines up with the layer below. A person who has it runs overlay targets, reads the error map and feeds corrections back to the scanner.
skills.learned: On the job in a litho or metrology area.

skills.name: Ellipsometry
skills.what: Measuring the thickness and optical constants of thin films from the way they change polarized light. A person who has it picks the film model, runs the map and judges whether the fit can be trusted.
skills.learned: On the job in a fab metrology or thin films area.

skills.name: Four-Point Probe Measurement
skills.what: Measuring sheet resistance of a doped or metal layer with four in-line probes. A person who has it maps a monitor wafer and reads uniformity as a check on implant dose, anneal or film thickness.
skills.learned: On the job in implant, diffusion and metals areas.

skills.name: Thin Film Stress Measurement
skills.what: Finding the stress in a deposited film from how much it bows the wafer. A person who has it measures curvature before and after deposition and reports tensile or compressive stress.
skills.learned: On the job in thin films and metrology.

skills.name: Particle Count Monitoring
skills.what: Counting particles in cleanroom air, in process liquids and on monitor wafers run through a tool. A person who has it runs the checks on schedule and holds a tool that adds too many.
skills.learned: On the job in a fab.

skills.name: Wafer Defect Inspection
skills.what: Scanning wafers for particles, scratches and pattern defects at set points in the process flow. A person who has it runs inspection recipes, reads the defect map and holds a lot that exceeds its limit.
skills.learned: On the job in a defect or yield area.

skills.name: Defect SEM Review
skills.what: Revisiting defects found by inspection in an electron microscope to see what each one is. A person who has it drives to the coordinates, images the defect and takes an elemental spectrum when the source is unclear.
skills.learned: On the job in a defect area.

skills.name: Defect Classification
skills.what: Sorting defects into types, such as particle, scratch, residue, bridge or void, by hand or by training an automatic classifier. A person who has it keeps classes consistent enough that a rise in one type points at a tool.
skills.learned: On the job in a defect or yield area.

skills.name: Wafer Map Analysis
skills.what: Reading the pattern of failing dies or defects across a wafer, such as edge rings, scratches, clusters and repeaters, and tracing it to a process step or tool. A person who has it stacks maps across lots and compares tool histories.
skills.learned: On the job as a yield or test technician or engineer.

skills.name: Chemical Vapor Deposition
skills.what: Depositing thin films on wafers from reacting gases. A person who has it runs deposition recipes, checks thickness and uniformity on monitors and recognizes a chamber that needs cleaning or seasoning.
skills.learned: On the job through tool certification; semiconductor manufacturing programs teach the principles.

skills.name: LPCVD
skills.what: Depositing polysilicon, nitride and oxide films on batches of wafers in a low-pressure furnace tube. A person who has it loads boats, runs the recipe and checks thickness across the boat and from run to run.
skills.learned: On the job in a diffusion area.

skills.name: PECVD
skills.what: Depositing dielectric films with a plasma so the wafer can stay at a lower temperature. A person who has it runs deposition and chamber clean recipes and tracks thickness, uniformity, stress and particles.
skills.learned: On the job in a thin films area.

skills.name: Atomic Layer Deposition
skills.what: Building a film one atomic layer at a time by alternating precursor pulses and purges. A person who has it runs ALD recipes, keeps precursor delivery stable and verifies thickness to a few angstroms.
skills.learned: On the job in a thin films area.

skills.name: Epitaxial Growth
skills.what: Growing a single-crystal layer of silicon or silicon-germanium on a wafer. A person who has it runs the pre-clean and growth recipes and checks thickness, doping and crystal defects.
skills.learned: On the job in an epitaxy area.
tools: Hydrogen, silane and chlorosilane gas systems
Four-point probes and film thickness tools

skills.name: PVD Sputtering
skills.what: Depositing metal films by knocking atoms off a target with argon plasma. A person who has it runs sputter recipes, tracks target life and checks sheet resistance and uniformity.
skills.learned: On the job in a metals area.

skills.name: Barrier and Seed Layer Deposition
skills.what: Sputtering the thin barrier and copper seed that line trenches and vias before copper fill. A person who has it tunes for coverage on the sidewalls and bottom of deep features.
skills.learned: On the job as a metals process technician or engineer.

skills.name: Plasma Etching
skills.what: Removing material from a wafer with a reactive plasma to transfer the resist pattern into the film below. A person who has it runs etch recipes, checks depth and line width afterwards and keeps the chamber in condition between cleans.
skills.learned: On the job through tool certification; semiconductor manufacturing programs teach the principles.
tools: Fluorine, chlorine and bromine process gases

skills.name: Reactive Ion Etching
skills.what: Plasma etching in which ions are driven straight down at the wafer, giving vertical sidewalls. A person who has it balances pressure, power and gas mix for etch rate, profile and selectivity to the mask.
skills.learned: On the job in an etch area.

skills.name: Inductively Coupled Plasma Etching
skills.what: Etching with a high-density plasma whose density and ion energy are set separately by source and bias power. A person who has it uses that control for deep or highly selective etches.
skills.learned: On the job as an experienced etch technician or engineer.

skills.name: Endpoint Detection
skills.what: Setting up and reading the signal that tells an etch or polish to stop at the right layer. A person who has it picks the wavelength or signal to watch and sets the algorithm so the stop is neither early nor late.
skills.learned: On the job as an etch or polish technician or engineer.
tools: Motor current and eddy current endpoint on polishers

skills.name: Wet Bench Processing
skills.what: Cleaning and etching wafers in chemical baths or single-wafer spray tools. A person who has it runs the clean sequence, tracks bath life and concentration and handles acids safely.
skills.learned: On the job in a wet process area.
tools: SC1, SC2, hydrofluoric acid and sulfuric-peroxide chemistries

skills.name: Wet Chemical Etching
skills.what: Removing a film in a liquid etchant chosen to attack it and spare what lies beneath. A person who has it controls time, temperature and bath age for the etch rate and checks for undercut.
skills.learned: On the job in a wet process area.

skills.name: Ion Implantation
skills.what: Driving dopant ions into a wafer at a set energy and dose. A person who has it runs implant recipes, confirms species, dose and tilt, and works safely around high voltage and toxic source gases.
skills.learned: On the job through tool certification.

skills.name: Thermal Oxidation
skills.what: Growing silicon dioxide on wafers in a furnace with oxygen or steam. A person who has it loads boats, runs the recipe and checks oxide thickness and uniformity.
skills.learned: On the job in a diffusion area.

skills.name: Furnace Annealing
skills.what: Heating batches of wafers in a controlled atmosphere to repair implant damage, drive dopants in or densify films. A person who has it runs the recipe and confirms the result on monitor wafers.
skills.learned: On the job in a diffusion area.

skills.name: Rapid Thermal Processing
skills.what: Heating a single wafer for seconds with lamps to activate dopants or form silicides without letting them spread. A person who has it runs spike and soak anneals and keeps the temperature measurement calibrated.
skills.learned: On the job in an implant or diffusion area.

skills.name: Chemical Mechanical Planarization
skills.what: Polishing a wafer flat with slurry on a rotating pad. A person who has it runs polish recipes, changes pads and conditioners, and checks removal, dishing and scratches.
skills.learned: On the job through tool certification.

skills.name: Fault Detection and Classification
skills.what: Watching the sensor traces of a process tool, such as pressures, powers, flows and temperatures, to catch a run that drifts from normal. A person who has it sets limits and models, and follows an alarm back to the hardware at fault.
skills.learned: On the job as an equipment or process engineer.

skills.name: Die Attach
skills.what: Picking dies from a sawn wafer and bonding them to a leadframe or substrate with epoxy, film or solder. A person who has it sets dispense pattern, placement and bond force and checks coverage, tilt and bondline thickness.
skills.learned: On the job at an assembly and test plant; die bonder makers' training.

skills.name: Wafer Dicing
skills.what: Cutting a finished wafer into individual dies. A person who has it mounts the wafer on tape, aligns to the streets, sets blade, speed and water and checks for chipping and cracks.
skills.learned: On the job at an assembly and test plant.

skills.name: Wire Bonding
skills.what: Connecting a die to its package with fine wire, by ball bonding or wedge bonding. A person who has it sets force, ultrasonic power, time and temperature, programs the loops and checks bonds by pull and shear.
skills.learned: On the job at an assembly and test plant; bonder makers' training.

skills.name: Copper Wire Bonding
skills.what: Ball bonding with copper wire, which is harder than gold and oxidizes as the ball forms. A person who has it runs forming gas at the bond head and tunes the bond to avoid damaging the pad beneath.
skills.learned: On the job after gold wire bonding experience.
tools: Wire bonders with forming gas kits

skills.name: Flip Chip Bonding
skills.what: Mounting a die face down so its solder bumps join directly to the substrate. A person who has it sets flux, placement accuracy and the reflow or thermocompression profile and checks for opens and bridges.
skills.learned: On the job at an advanced packaging plant.

skills.name: Underfill Dispensing
skills.what: Flowing epoxy under a flip chip die to lock the solder joints against stress. A person who has it sets dispense pattern, volume and substrate temperature so the gap fills without voids and the fillet is even.
skills.learned: On the job at a packaging plant.

skills.name: Transfer Molding
skills.what: Encapsulating bonded dies by forcing heated epoxy mold compound into a mold around them. A person who has it sets temperature, transfer pressure and cure time and checks for voids, wire sweep and incomplete fill.
skills.learned: On the job at a packaging plant.

skills.name: Bond Pull and Shear Testing
skills.what: Checking wire bond and die attach strength by pulling wires with a hook and shearing balls and dies with a tool. A person who has it reads the force and the failure mode against the limits, which in military and aerospace work come from MIL-STD-883.
skills.learned: On the job at a packaging plant.
tools: Bond testers such as Nordson Dage

skills.name: Wafer Probe Testing
skills.what: Testing every die on a wafer electrically before it is cut. A person who has it loads the probe card, sets up the prober, checks contact and cleans the probe tips, and judges whether a bad map is the wafer or the setup.
skills.learned: On the job at a fab or test plant.

skills.name: Semiconductor Final Test
skills.what: Testing packaged devices on automatic test equipment and sorting them into bins. A person who has it sets up the handler and load board, runs the program and tells a real failure from a contact or setup problem.
skills.learned: On the job at a test plant; tester makers' training for those who write test programs.

skills.name: Electrical Fault Isolation
skills.what: Finding the physical spot in a chip that causes an electrical failure. A person who has it uses light emission, laser stimulation and thermal imaging to localize the fault before the device is cut open.
skills.learned: Engineering degree and on-the-job training in a failure analysis lab.

skills.name: FIB Cross-Sectioning
skills.what: Cutting into a chip at an exact spot with a focused ion beam and imaging the exposed layers. A person who has it protects the surface, mills and polishes the face and takes a clear image.
skills.learned: On the job in a failure analysis or process lab; microscope makers' training.

skills.name: TEM Sample Preparation
skills.what: Cutting and thinning a slice of a device until electrons pass through it, for imaging in a transmission electron microscope. A person who has it lifts out a lamella from the right place and thins it without damage.
skills.learned: On the job in a failure analysis or materials lab.

skills.name: SIMS Analysis
skills.what: Measuring how dopants and impurities are distributed with depth by sputtering the surface and analyzing the ions that come off. A person who has it sets up the measurement and turns it into a concentration profile using standards.
skills.learned: Science or engineering degree and on-the-job training in a materials lab.

skills.name: Electrode Slurry Mixing
skills.what: Mixing active material, binder, conductive additive and solvent into a uniform slurry for coating. A person who has it weighs and adds in order, runs the mixer program and checks viscosity, solids content and fineness before release.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Electrode Coating
skills.what: Coating slurry onto copper or aluminum foil and drying it in a long oven. A person who has it sets the die gap, pump and line speed, and holds coat weight, edges and alignment between the two sides.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Dry Electrode Coating
skills.what: Making an electrode without solvent, by forming dry powder into a film and laminating it to foil. A person who has it controls powder feed, roll gap and temperature so the film is even and holds together.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant that uses the process.

skills.name: Electrode Calendering
skills.what: Pressing a coated electrode between rolls to its target thickness and density. A person who has it sets roll gap, force and temperature and checks thickness, wrinkles and foil stretch.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Electrode Slitting
skills.what: Cutting a wide electrode roll into narrow strips. A person who has it sets up the knives, holds width and watches for burrs and dust that could short a cell.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Separator Handling
skills.what: Unwinding and feeding the thin porous film that keeps the electrodes apart. A person who has it controls tension and tracking and catches wrinkles, tears and contamination.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Cell Winding
skills.what: Winding anode, separator and cathode into a jelly roll with exact alignment. A person who has it sets tension and edge guidance, checks overhang and resistance-tests the roll for shorts.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Jelly Roll Can Insertion
skills.what: Placing a wound electrode assembly into its can without scraping or deforming it. A person who has it runs the insertion station and checks for damage and seating depth.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Electrode Tab Welding
skills.what: Welding electrode foils or tabs to the cell's terminals, by ultrasonic or laser welding. A person who has it sets energy, pressure and amplitude and proves weld strength by pull test.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Electrolyte Filling
skills.what: Dosing electrolyte into a cell under vacuum in a dry room so it soaks the electrodes fully. A person who has it runs the fill cycle, verifies fill weight and works safely with a flammable, moisture-sensitive liquid.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Cell Sealing
skills.what: Closing a filled cell for good, by laser welding the cap or crimping the can. A person who has it sets up the weld or crimp and checks each seal for leaks.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Cell Formation
skills.what: Giving a new cell its first controlled charge and discharge cycles, which build the protective layer on the anode. A person who has it loads trays, runs the protocol and pulls cells whose voltage or temperature goes outside limits.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Cell Degassing
skills.what: Releasing the gas a cell produces during formation and resealing it. A person who has it runs the degas step under vacuum and checks the final seal.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Cell Aging
skills.what: Resting formed cells for days at a set temperature and measuring how far their voltage falls, to find cells with internal shorts. A person who has it manages the storage lots and reads the voltage-drop data.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Cell Grading
skills.what: Measuring each cell's capacity, voltage and internal resistance and sorting cells into matched groups. A person who has it runs the grading equipment and holds the sort limits.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Cell Voltage Monitoring
skills.what: Measuring individual cell voltages in a tray, module or pack and checking the sense wiring that carries them. A person who has it finds an open or crossed sense line and a cell that is out of balance.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell or pack plant.

skills.name: Battery Module Assembly
skills.what: Building cells into a module: placing cells, adhesive and cooling parts, then welding or bolting the connections. A person who has it works under high-voltage rules and checks polarity at every step.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack plant, after high-voltage safety qualification.

skills.name: Battery Pack Assembly
skills.what: Installing modules, busbars, cooling, electronics and harnesses into a pack enclosure and closing it. A person who has it follows the torque and connection sequence and records each high-voltage joint.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack plant, after high-voltage safety qualification.

skills.name: Busbar Installation
skills.what: Fitting the rigid conductors that carry current between cells, modules and pack terminals. A person who has it keeps joint surfaces clean, torques or welds each joint and checks its resistance.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack or power electronics plant.

skills.name: Cell Interconnect Welding
skills.what: Welding cell terminals to current collectors or busbars, usually by laser. A person who has it keeps the parts clamped tight, checks weld position and depth and proves strength and resistance on samples.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack plant.

skills.name: High-Voltage Harness Installation
skills.what: Routing and connecting the orange high-voltage cables of a pack or vehicle. A person who has it seats and locks each connector, torques terminals and confirms the interlock circuit is complete.
skills.learned: On the job, after high-voltage safety qualification.

skills.name: Battery Management System Installation
skills.what: Fitting the battery management electronics and their sense wiring to a module or pack and checking that every cell voltage and temperature reads correctly. A person who has it loads the configuration and clears wiring faults.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack plant.

skills.name: Battery Pack Cooling System Assembly
skills.what: Installing the cold plates, manifolds and hoses that carry coolant through a pack. A person who has it makes up each connection and pressure-tests the circuit before the pack is closed.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack plant.

skills.name: Pack Enclosure Sealing
skills.what: Sealing a pack's lid and penetrations against water and dust. A person who has it lays the sealant bead or gasket without gaps, torques the lid in sequence and confirms the seal by leak test.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack plant.

skills.name: Pack Leak Testing
skills.what: Proving a pack's enclosure and coolant circuit are tight, by pressure decay or helium. A person who has it connects the tester, runs the cycle and finds the leak path when a pack fails.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack plant.

skills.name: Battery Pack End-of-Line Testing
skills.what: Running a finished pack through its final electrical test: isolation, contactors, communication, voltage and a charge and discharge pulse. A person who has it connects the pack safely and reads a failure back to the part at fault.
skills.learned: On the job at a pack plant, after high-voltage safety qualification.

skills.name: Stator Winding
skills.what: Putting copper windings into a motor stator and connecting the phases. A person who has it runs the winding, inserting and forming equipment and checks resistance and insulation.
skills.learned: On the job at a motor plant.

skills.name: Hairpin Insertion
skills.what: Forming flat copper wire into hairpins, inserting them into stator slots and twisting the ends ready for welding. A person who has it runs the forming and insertion stations without scraping the wire's insulation.
skills.learned: On the job at a motor plant.
tools: Hairpin forming, insertion and twisting machines

skills.name: Hairpin Welding
skills.what: Laser welding pairs of hairpin ends to complete a stator's winding. A person who has it keeps ends stripped and aligned, sets the weld and checks each joint for size and spatter.
skills.learned: On the job at a motor plant.

skills.name: Stator Impregnation and Potting
skills.what: Filling a stator's windings with resin to insulate them, hold them still and carry heat away. A person who has it preheats the stator, applies or trickles the resin and cures it without voids.
skills.learned: On the job at a motor plant.

skills.name: Rotor Magnet Installation
skills.what: Inserting permanent magnets into a rotor and fixing them with adhesive or resin. A person who has it handles strong magnets safely, keeps polarity right and checks each one is seated.
skills.learned: On the job at a motor plant.

skills.name: Electric Motor Assembly
skills.what: Putting a traction motor together: rotor into stator, bearings, housing, resolver and terminals. A person who has it guides the magnetized rotor in without contact and sets bearing fits and position sensor alignment.
skills.learned: On the job at a motor or drive unit plant.

skills.name: Motor Housing Assembly
skills.what: Fitting a stator into its housing and closing it with the end covers, seals and cooling connections. A person who has it heats the housing for the fit, seats the stator to depth and leak-tests the cooling jacket.
skills.learned: On the job at a motor or drive unit plant.

skills.name: Motor End-of-Line Testing
skills.what: Testing each finished motor or drive unit: insulation, resistance, back-EMF, noise and vibration, and performance under load. A person who has it runs the stand and tells a real failure from a fixture or connection fault.
skills.learned: On the job at a motor plant.

skills.name: Electrode Notching
skills.what: Cutting coated electrode into sheets with their tabs, by die or laser, for stacked cells. A person who has it sets the web path and cut registration, watches for burrs and loose particles and changes dies or optics before the edge degrades.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Cell Stacking
skills.what: Stacking anode, separator and cathode sheets, or folding separator between them, into the electrode stack of a pouch or prismatic cell. A person who has it holds alignment and overhang within limits, clears a misfeed without damaging sheets and tests each stack for shorts.
skills.learned: On the job at a cell plant.

skills.name: Current Good Manufacturing Practice
skills.what: Working the way regulated drug, device and food plants must: follow the approved procedure exactly, record each step as it is done, in ink or a validated system, and report any deviation. A person who has it produces a batch record that an auditor can follow.
skills.learned: Employer training before touching product, refreshed yearly. The rules are in FDA regulations: 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211 for drugs, Part 820 for devices and Part 117 for food.

skills.name: Aseptic Technique
skills.what: Working with sterile product and components so nothing living gets in: slow movements, never reaching over open containers, sanitized gloves, first air kept clear. A person who has it passes a media fill and routine glove and gown monitoring.
skills.learned: Site training and qualification by media fill at a sterile manufacturing plant; microbiology lab courses teach the basics.

skills.name: Aseptic Filling
skills.what: Filling sterile product into sterile containers and closing them inside a controlled zone. A person who has it sets up the filler with sterilized parts, checks fill weights and stopper placement and makes only approved interventions.
skills.learned: On the job at a sterile fill plant, after aseptic gowning and media fill qualification.

skills.name: Environmental Monitoring
skills.what: Sampling the air, surfaces and people in a clean manufacturing area for particles and microbes. A person who has it takes samples at the mapped sites without contaminating them and knows the alert and action limits.
skills.learned: On the job in a pharmaceutical quality or microbiology group.

skills.name: Lyophilization
skills.what: Freeze drying a product: freezing it on the shelves, then pulling vacuum so the ice leaves as vapor. A person who has it loads the dryer aseptically, runs the cycle and checks shelf temperature and chamber pressure through each stage.
skills.learned: On the job at a sterile fill plant.

skills.name: Granulation and Blending
skills.what: Turning drug and filler powders into a uniform, free-flowing blend for tableting. A person who has it charges by weight, runs the granulator, dryer, mill and blender to the batch record and samples for moisture and uniformity.
skills.learned: On the job at a solid-dose pharmaceutical plant.

skills.name: Tablet Compression
skills.what: Running a rotary tablet press. A person who has it sets fill depth and compression force, checks weight, thickness, hardness and friability at intervals and corrects sticking, capping and weight drift.
skills.learned: On the job at a solid-dose pharmaceutical or supplement plant.

skills.name: Tablet Film Coating
skills.what: Spraying a thin polymer coat onto tablets tumbling in a heated pan. A person who has it balances spray rate, air temperature and pan speed, and checks weight gain and appearance.
skills.learned: On the job at a solid-dose pharmaceutical plant.

skills.name: Steam Sterilization
skills.what: Sterilizing product, components or equipment with saturated steam under pressure. A person who has it loads to the validated pattern, runs the cycle and reviews temperature, time and biological indicator results before release.
skills.learned: On the job in pharmaceutical and device plants. Cycles are validated to ISO 17665.

skills.name: Ethylene Oxide Sterilization
skills.what: Sterilizing heat-sensitive medical devices with ethylene oxide gas. A person who has it runs preconditioning, gas exposure and aeration, handles a toxic and flammable gas safely and reviews the cycle record.
skills.learned: On the job at a device or contract sterilization plant. Cycles are validated to ISO 11135.

skills.name: Process Validation
skills.what: Proving by a written protocol that equipment is installed correctly, operates across its range and makes good product every time (installation, operational and performance qualification). A person who has it executes protocol steps, records data and raises deviations.
skills.learned: On the job in a validation or quality group at a regulated plant.

skills.name: HPLC Analysis
skills.what: Measuring how much of a drug or impurity is in a sample by liquid chromatography. A person who has it prepares mobile phase, standards and samples, runs system suitability and integrates peaks to the method.
skills.learned: A chemistry degree or laboratory technology program, then method training on the job.

skills.name: Gas Chromatography
skills.what: Separating and measuring volatile compounds, such as residual solvents, by gas chromatography. A person who has it prepares standards and samples, sets the method and checks system suitability.
skills.learned: A chemistry degree or laboratory technology program, then method training on the job.
tools: Gas chromatographs with flame ionization detectors

skills.name: Dissolution Testing
skills.what: Measuring how fast a tablet or capsule releases its drug in a stirred vessel. A person who has it sets up the apparatus, pulls samples at the time points and analyzes them. The method is USP chapter 711.
skills.learned: Laboratory technology program or chemistry degree; on the job in a quality control lab.
tools: Dissolution baths with paddles and baskets

skills.name: Karl Fischer Titration
skills.what: Measuring small amounts of water in a sample by titration. A person who has it standardizes the reagent, handles samples so they pick up no moisture and reports the result.
skills.learned: Laboratory technology program or chemistry degree; on the job in a quality control lab.
tools: Volumetric and coulometric Karl Fischer titrators

skills.name: Endotoxin Testing
skills.what: Testing injectable products and water for bacterial endotoxin with the LAL assay. A person who has it prepares standards and dilutions in endotoxin-free ware and runs gel-clot or kinetic methods. The method is USP chapter 85.
skills.learned: Microbiology degree or laboratory program; on the job in a quality control lab.

skills.name: Sterility Testing
skills.what: Testing whether a sterile product contains any living organism, by filtering or inoculating it into growth media and incubating for 14 days. A person who has it works in an isolator or clean hood so the test itself adds nothing. The method is USP chapter 71.
skills.learned: Microbiology degree or laboratory program; on the job in a quality control lab.

skills.name: Microbial Enumeration Testing
skills.what: Counting the bacteria, yeast and mold in a product, ingredient or device by plating and incubating samples. A person who has it prepares dilutions, plates them, counts colonies and reports against the limit.
skills.learned: Microbiology degree or laboratory program; on the job in a food or pharmaceutical lab.

skills.name: HACCP Food Safety
skills.what: Running the part of a hazard analysis and critical control point plan that sits at your station: checking the critical limit, recording it and acting when it is missed. A person who has it knows the plant's critical control points and why each exists.
skills.learned: Employer training; HACCP courses accredited by the International HACCP Alliance. Under FDA rules a plant's food safety plan is overseen by a Preventive Controls Qualified Individual.

skills.name: Sanitation Procedures
skills.what: Cleaning and sanitizing food equipment to the written procedure: disassemble, rinse, wash, rinse, inspect, sanitize. A person who has it verifies the result by inspection and swab before the line restarts.
skills.learned: On the job at a food plant.

skills.name: Allergen Changeover Cleaning
skills.what: Keeping allergens out of products that do not declare them. A person who has it follows the schedule and segregation rules, does the full allergen clean at changeover and verifies it with a test swab.
skills.learned: On the job at a food plant.

skills.name: Food Batching and Blending
skills.what: Weighing ingredients to a formula and blending or cooking the batch. A person who has it scales in the right order, runs the mixer or kettle to time and temperature, checks the batch against target, such as dissolved sugar by a temperature-corrected Brix reading, adjusts it and records each lot number used.
skills.learned: On the job at a food or beverage plant.

skills.name: Clean-in-Place Operation
skills.what: Cleaning tanks, pipes and fillers without taking them apart, by circulating rinse, caustic, acid and sanitizer. A person who has it runs the cycle and confirms time, temperature, concentration and flow were met.
skills.learned: On the job at a food, beverage or pharmaceutical plant.

skills.name: Pasteurization
skills.what: Heating a liquid product to a set temperature for a set time to kill harmful organisms, then cooling it. A person who has it runs the pasteurizer, checks the holding temperature and flow diversion and keeps the legal records.
skills.learned: On the job at a dairy, juice or beverage plant. Milk plants work to the Grade A Pasteurized Milk Ordinance.

skills.name: Retort Operation
skills.what: Sterilizing sealed cans, jars and pouches with steam or hot water under pressure. A person who has it vents and runs the retort to the scheduled process and records time, temperature and pressure for every load.
skills.learned: On the job. For low-acid canned foods, FDA requires retort operations to be supervised by someone who has completed a Better Process Control School.

skills.name: Bottle and Can Filling
skills.what: Running a filler for bottles or cans. A person who has it sets fill level and speed, changes over for size, checks closures and codes and clears jams safely.
skills.learned: On the job at a beverage or food plant.

skills.name: Can Seaming
skills.what: Closing cans with a double seam that stays airtight. A person who has it tears seams down at intervals, measures overlap and tightness and adjusts the seaming rolls.
skills.learned: On the job at a canning plant; seamer and can makers run seam evaluation courses.

skills.name: Beverage Carbonation
skills.what: Dissolving carbon dioxide in a beverage to its specified level. A person who has it controls product temperature and pressure and tests carbonation on filled packages.
skills.learned: On the job at a beverage plant.

skills.name: Spray Drying
skills.what: Turning a liquid into powder by atomizing it into hot air. A person who has it balances feed rate and inlet and outlet air temperatures for the right moisture and manages the dust explosion hazard.
skills.learned: On the job at a dairy, food or chemical plant.
tools: Spray dryers with nozzle or rotary atomizers

skills.name: Packaging Line Operation
skills.what: Running the machines at the end of a line: cartoners, case packers, coders, wrappers and palletizers. A person who has it changes over for a new size, keeps materials fed and clears jams safely.
skills.learned: On the job; the packaging machinery association PMMI offers mechatronics certificates for packaging technicians.

skills.name: Metal Detection and Checkweighing
skills.what: Running the in-line checks that reject packages that are off weight or carry metal or other foreign material. A person who has it challenges each device with test pieces on schedule and holds product when a check fails.
skills.learned: On the job at a food or pharmaceutical packaging line.

skills.name: Weighing and Dispensing
skills.what: Weighing out each raw material for a batch in a dispensing booth, to the batch record. A person who has it checks identity and lot against the record, verifies the balance, weighs within tolerance, labels each container and has a second person verify.
skills.learned: On the job at a pharmaceutical plant, in the first weeks, under good manufacturing practice.
tools: Batch records or an electronic batch system

skills.name: Electrical Schematic Reading
skills.what: Reading electrical drawings: power distribution, control circuits, ladder diagrams and wiring diagrams. A person who has it traces a circuit from source to load, finds a device on the drawing and in the panel and knows what state each contact should be in.
skills.learned: Electrical and mechatronics programs at community colleges; electrical apprenticeships.

skills.name: Multimeter Testing
skills.what: Measuring voltage, current, resistance and continuity safely with a digital multimeter. A person who has it picks the function and range, places leads correctly and reads what the result says about the circuit.
skills.learned: Taught first in electrical, electronics and maintenance programs.

skills.name: Oscilloscope Measurement
skills.what: Viewing electrical signals over time on an oscilloscope. A person who has it sets time base, voltage scale and trigger, uses the right probe and reads amplitude, frequency, rise time and noise.
skills.learned: Electronics technology programs; on the job.

skills.name: 480 V Power Distribution
skills.what: Working on a plant's three-phase power: switchgear, transformers, motor control centers and feeders. A person who has it reads a one-line diagram, switches and isolates equipment safely and tests it dead before work.
skills.learned: Electrical apprenticeship leading to a journeyman license; employer qualified-person training under NFPA 70E.

skills.name: Three-Phase Motor Wiring
skills.what: Connecting three-phase motors and their starters. A person who has it reads the nameplate, makes the wye or delta connection for the supply voltage, sets overload protection and checks rotation.
skills.learned: Electrical apprenticeships and industrial maintenance programs.

skills.name: Motor Control Troubleshooting
skills.what: Finding why a motor will not start, stop or run right. A person who has it works through the control circuit with a meter and the schematic, from the interlocks and overloads to the contactor and the motor.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance and electrical programs; on the job.

skills.name: Conduit Bending
skills.what: Bending and installing electrical conduit. A person who has it makes accurate 90s, offsets and saddles, keeps the total bend between pull points within the code limit and supports the run.
skills.learned: Electrical apprenticeship.

skills.name: Insulation Resistance Testing
skills.what: Testing the insulation of motors, cables and windings with a megohmmeter. A person who has it isolates the equipment, applies the right test voltage, corrects for temperature and trends the result.
skills.learned: Electrical apprenticeships and maintenance programs; on the job.

skills.name: Sensor and I/O Wiring
skills.what: Wiring sensors and actuators to a controller's inputs and outputs. A person who has it knows sourcing from sinking, wires and terminates to the drawing, labels each wire and checks every point from the device to the controller.
skills.learned: Mechatronics and electrical programs; on the job as a panel builder or controls technician.

skills.name: PLC Programming
skills.what: Writing programs for programmable logic controllers, most often in ladder diagram: configuring the controller and its I/O, then contacts, coils, timers, counters, compares and sequences. A person who has it can turn a machine's sequence of operations into working, readable logic and go online, edit and download safely.
skills.learned: Mechatronics and automation programs at community colleges; PLC makers' and distributors' courses.

skills.name: PLC Troubleshooting
skills.what: Going online with a running controller to find why a machine has stopped. A person who has it follows the logic to the condition that is not met, then to the sensor, wire or output behind it, without changing the program.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance programs; on the job.

skills.name: Structured Text Programming
skills.what: Writing controller logic as text, with expressions, IF and CASE statements and loops, where ladder would be awkward. A person who has it writes maths, state machines and data handling in the IEC 61131-3 language.
skills.learned: Automation engineering courses and PLC makers' training.

skills.name: HMI Development
skills.what: Building the operator screens of a machine: displays, buttons, alarms, trends and recipes tied to controller tags. A person who has it lays out screens an operator can read at a glance and act on.
skills.learned: Automation programs and software makers' courses.

skills.name: OPC UA Integration
skills.what: Connecting controllers and machines to plant software through OPC UA. A person who has it configures servers and clients, maps tags, sets security certificates and checks that data arrives.
skills.learned: On the job as a controls or manufacturing systems engineer.
tools: OPC UA servers such as Kepware

skills.name: Industrial Network Troubleshooting
skills.what: Finding faults on the networks that tie controllers, drives and I/O together. A person who has it checks addresses, switches, cables and connectors and reads device and switch diagnostics.
skills.learned: Automation programs; on the job.

skills.name: CAN Bus Diagnostics
skills.what: Checking the controller area network that links a vehicle's or machine's electronic units. A person who has it measures bus resistance and voltage, reads the traffic with an interface and finds a missing node or a wiring fault.
skills.learned: Automotive and electronics programs; on the job in test.

skills.name: Variable Frequency Drive Setup
skills.what: Commissioning the drive that sets an AC motor's speed. A person who has it enters motor data, sets ramps, limits and control source, tunes it to the load and reads fault codes.
skills.learned: Industrial maintenance and electrical programs; drive makers' courses.

skills.name: Servo Drive Configuration
skills.what: Setting up a servo axis: motor and feedback, limits, scaling, homing and the link to the motion controller. A person who has it brings an axis from wiring to its first controlled move.
skills.learned: Automation programs; drive makers' courses.

skills.name: Servo Tuning
skills.what: Adjusting a servo loop's gains and filters so the axis follows its command quickly without overshoot or ringing. A person who has it reads the following error, runs the autotune and finishes by hand.
skills.learned: On the job as a controls or motion engineer; drive makers' courses.

skills.name: Instrumentation Calibration
skills.what: Checking and adjusting process transmitters for pressure, temperature, flow and level against a traceable standard. A person who has it runs a multi-point check, adjusts zero and span and records readings as found and as left.
