A person who has it checks dew point and drying time before a run, keeps materials and colors from being mixed up and knows the defects wet resin makes.
skills.learned: On the job in molding and extrusion plants, and in plastics processing courses at community colleges.
tools: Dew point meters and moisture analyzers

skills.name: Thermoforming
skills.what: Forming heated plastic sheet over or into a mold by vacuum, air pressure and plug assist, then trimming the parts from the web. A person who has it sets oven zones, forming and cooling times and the trim press, and corrects thin corners, webbing, blush and poor detail.
skills.learned: On the job in packaging and custom thermoforming plants, with short courses from equipment makers and plastics associations.

skills.name: Plastic Welding
skills.what: Joining molded plastic parts, films and nonwovens by ultrasonic, hot plate, spin, vibration or laser welding, and staking and sealing them ultrasonically. A person who has it sets amplitude, force, energy, time or collapse distance for the joint, holds the weld window, proves strength by a pull, burst or cross-section test rather than by look, and keeps horns, nests and fixtures in condition.
skills.learned: On the job in molding, medical device, automotive plastics and nonwovens plants; the welders' makers run training.
tools: Hot plate, spin and vibration welders

skills.name: Extrusion Line Setup and Troubleshooting
skills.what: Setting up an extrusion line and finding the cause when it makes bad product: changing dies, screws, screen packs and sizing tooling, centering the die and profiling gauge with die bolts and air ring, and tracing gels, die lines, gauge bands and melt fracture to temperature, pressure, material or tooling. A person who has it brings a line from cold to good product on a new order and fixes a defect from the process data rather than by turning knobs.
skills.learned: Years on extrusion lines, with process courses from equipment makers and plastics associations.
tools: Die bolt and air ring adjustment tools

skills.name: Rubber Extrusion and Calendering
skills.what: Forming uncured rubber compound into continuous shapes: extruding treads, sidewalls, hose and seal profiles through a die, and calendering sheet or coating fabric and steel cord between heated rolls. A person who has it holds gauge, width and weight to the specification, keeps stock from scorching, and cools, cuts and stores the green stock so it builds.
skills.learned: On the job in tire and rubber products plants.

skills.name: Rubber Mixing and Milling
skills.what: Making rubber compound: weighing polymer, fillers, oils and curatives to the recipe, mixing them in an internal mixer by time, temperature and power, then sheeting, cooling and batching off on a two-roll mill. A person who has it holds dump temperature so the batch does not scorch, keeps curatives out of the wrong stage and has each batch tested before release.
skills.learned: On the job in tire and rubber products plants.

skills.name: Rubber Molding and Curing
skills.what: Vulcanizing rubber into its finished shape in a heated mold: loading preforms into compression, transfer or injection presses, or green tires into curing presses, running the cure to time, temperature and pressure, demolding and deflashing. A person who has it spots undercure, porosity, non-fill and flash, and changes mold inserts and bladders as the job calls for.
skills.learned: On the job in rubber goods and tire plants.
tools: Compression, transfer and rubber injection presses

skills.name: Tire Building
skills.what: Building a green tire on a building drum from its components: inner liner, body plies, beads, belts and tread, each placed, spliced and stitched to the specification, then transferred and shaped. A person who has it builds to weight and green-tire specification at rate, and knows which splice and placement defects become a scrapped tire after cure.
skills.learned: On the job: several weeks of training on the building machine before working to rate.
tools: Single-stage and automated tire building machines

skills.name: Glass Defect Inspection
skills.what: Finding and naming the defects in glass: stones, seeds, blisters, cords, checks and chips in containers, and scratches, roller wave, distortion and edge damage in flat and tempered glass. A person who has it inspects at the right light and distance, measures against the limits, and knows which station a defect comes from.
skills.learned: On the job in a glass plant. The National Glass Association's courses cover tempered glass inspection.

skills.name: Flat Glass Cutting
skills.what: Cutting sheets of float glass to size and shape on CNC cutting tables: loading the stock, running the optimized cut list, scoring and breaking out, and labeling each piece for the next station. A person who has it sets cutting pressure and oil for the glass's thickness and coating, and breaks out without flaring or shelling the edge.
skills.learned: On the job in a glass fabrication plant. The National Glass Association runs fabrication courses.
tools: CNC glass cutting and break-out tables

skills.name: Glass Container Forming
skills.what: Running an individual-section (IS) machine that forms bottles and jars from gobs of molten glass: setting the feeder and gob weight, adjusting section timing, swabbing the blank molds, changing molds, neck rings and plungers in a job change, and correcting forming defects. A person who has it keeps every section making good ware, and brings a section back after a stoppage without losing the job.
skills.learned: A forming apprenticeship of about 4,000 hours at a container glass plant.
tools: Blank and blow molds, neck rings and plungers

skills.name: Glass Edging and Drilling
skills.what: Grinding and polishing the edges of cut glass, and drilling holes and notches, on edgers, seamers, drills and CNC work centers before tempering. A person who has it gives each piece the edge the order calls for, and holds the size so the piece comes out of the furnace in tolerance.
skills.learned: On the job in a glass fabrication plant.

skills.name: Glass Laminating
skills.what: Bonding glass plies with a plastic interlayer into laminated safety glass: washing the glass, laying up the interlayer in a clean room, de-airing by nip rolls or vacuum, and finishing the bond in an autoclave. A person who has it keeps dirt and air out of the layup, and checks the bond for bubbles and delamination.
skills.learned: On the job in a laminating plant.
tools: Interlayer clean rooms and lay-up tables
Nip roll ovens and vacuum bag systems

skills.name: Glass Tempering
skills.what: Heat-strengthening and tempering flat glass in a horizontal tempering furnace: loading for the glass's size and coating, setting heat time, temperature and quench to its thickness, and checking stress, flatness and break pattern. A person who has it keeps roller wave and bow within limits, and proves the temper by the fragmentation test.
skills.learned: On the job at the furnace. The National Glass Association offers a Tempering Technician certificate course.

skills.name: Insulating Glass Unit Assembly
skills.what: Building sealed insulating glass units: washing the lites, applying the spacer, pressing and gas-filling the unit, applying the secondary seal, and checking size, gas fill and seal. A person who has it keeps the inside of the unit clean, the spacer square and the seal continuous.
skills.learned: On the job in an insulating glass plant.
tools: IG lines with washers, presses and gas fillers

skills.name: Corrugator Dry End Operation
skills.what: Running the dry end of a corrugator: the double backer that bonds the second liner on hot plates, the slitter-scorer, the cutoff knife and the stacker. A person who has it sets up order changes on the fly, controls warp and bond, and stacks board to length and score without crushing it.
skills.learned: On the job in a box plant; corrugator makers train operators.

skills.name: Corrugator Wet End Operation
skills.what: Running the wet end of a corrugator: the roll stands and splicers, the preheaters, and the single facers that flute the medium and glue it to a liner. A person who has it sets wrap and steam to suit the paper, holds glue roll gap and bridge tension, and splices rolls at speed without a break.
skills.learned: On the job in a box plant; corrugator makers and industry associations run box plant courses.

skills.name: Die Cutting
skills.what: Cutting and creasing paperboard, corrugated board or labels to shape with a steel-rule or rotary die. A person who has it mounts the die and makes it ready, sets pressure and the stripping and blanking tools, and holds cut register and crease quality through the run.
skills.learned: On the job in a folding carton, box or print finishing plant.

skills.name: Flexo Folder Gluer Operation
skills.what: Running the machine that prints, slots, folds and glues corrugated sheets into boxes in one pass. A person who has it mounts printing plates and dies, sets feed, print register, slotting and folding, holds glue joint and box dimensions, and changes over quickly between orders.
skills.learned: On the job in a box plant, as feeder, then catcher, then operator.
tools: Flexographic print units and anilox rolls

skills.name: Folder Gluer Operation
skills.what: Folding and gluing die-cut folding cartons or corrugated blanks on a folder gluer, in straight-line, crash-lock and four- and six-corner styles. A person who has it sets the feeder, prebreak, folding belts and glue guns, and checks cartons at speed for glue skips and fishtails.
skills.learned: On the job in a folding carton or box plant.

skills.name: Slitting and Rewinding
skills.what: Unwinding a large parent roll of paper, film or labels, slitting it to width and rewinding it into customer rolls. A person who has it sets knives and tension, holds roll hardness and edge quality, splices and changes cores, and checks rolls for defects before they ship.
skills.learned: On the job at a paper mill's winder or in a converting plant.

skills.name: Starch Adhesive Preparation
skills.what: Making the starch adhesive a corrugator bonds board with, in batch or continuous starch kitchens: water, starch, caustic and borax mixed to the recipe. A person who has it checks viscosity and gel temperature, adjusts the recipe for the board and the weather, and keeps the adhesive circulating without spoiling.
skills.learned: On the job in a box plant; starch suppliers train starch kitchen operators.

skills.name: Foil Stamping and Embossing
skills.what: Applying metallic foil, and raised or recessed images, to printed sheets with heated dies on a platen or cylinder press. A person who has it mounts dies and counter-dies, sets heat, pressure and dwell for the foil and the stock, and keeps register to the print.
skills.learned: On the job in a print finishing or packaging plant.

skills.name: Guillotine Cutting
skills.what: Cutting stacks of printed sheets to size on a programmable guillotine. A person who has it jogs and squares the lift, programs the cut sequence from the press sheet's marks, changes the knife and cutting stick, and uses the machine's safety devices correctly.
skills.learned: On the job in a bindery.

skills.name: Perfect Binding
skills.what: Binding gathered signatures into a book with a glued spine and a wrapped cover. A person who has it sets the gatherer, spine milling, glue (hot melt or PUR) and cover scoring, and checks page pull strength and squareness.
skills.learned: On the job in a book or commercial bindery.
tools: Hot melt and PUR glue units

skills.name: Saddle Stitching
skills.what: Gathering folded signatures over a saddle, stapling them through the spine and trimming the book on three sides. A person who has it sets the pockets, stitch heads and three-knife trimmer, and catches missing or doubled signatures.
skills.learned: On the job in a bindery.

skills.name: Sheet Folding
skills.what: Folding printed sheets into signatures and finished pieces on buckle and knife folders. A person who has it sets the folding plates, rollers and knives for the imposition, keeps signatures square and in register, and scores heavy stock so it does not crack.
skills.learned: On the job in a bindery.

skills.name: Channel Letter Fabrication
skills.what: Building the illuminated letters and logos of a sign: bending aluminum coil into returns by hand or on a channel letter bender, joining them to backs, fitting routed or formed faces and trim cap, so each letter is true to the artwork and light-tight. A person who has it builds a set of letters that mount, wire and light without rework.
skills.learned: On the job in a sign plant; bender makers train operators.

skills.name: Illuminated Sign Wiring
skills.what: Wiring the lighting of an electric sign: laying out and mounting LED modules, running wire to power supplies, adding the disconnect and grounding, and labeling the sign so it can be listed to UL 48 and installed under NEC Article 600. A person who has it wires a sign that lights evenly, passes the listing inspection and can be serviced.
skills.learned: On the job in a sign plant, under the procedures of the plant's UL listing.

skills.name: Large-Format Digital Printing
skills.what: Printing graphics, banners, wraps and sign faces on wide-format inkjet printers: preparing the file in the RIP, choosing media and color profile, running the printer and laminating or cutting the prints. A person who has it prints to the proof's color, without banding or head strikes, and keeps the heads and media path clean.
skills.learned: On the job in a sign or print shop; printer makers' courses.

skills.name: Vinyl Graphics Application
skills.what: Cutting vinyl graphics on a plotter, weeding and masking them, and applying cut or printed vinyl to sign faces, glass, walls and vehicles without bubbles, wrinkles or stretch. A person who has it places a graphic square and to position and works it over curves and rivets so it stays down.
skills.learned: On the job in a sign shop; film makers certify graphics and wrap installers.

skills.name: Dental Model and Die Preparation
skills.what: Turning an impression or a scan into the working model a restoration is made on: pouring and trimming stone models or printing them, sectioning and pinning dies, trimming margins and mounting the models on an articulator. A person who has it leaves a model whose margins are clear and whose bite is the patient's.
skills.learned: On the job as a model technician, the usual first job in a dental laboratory; dental laboratory technology programs.

skills.name: Dental CAD Design
skills.what: Designing crowns, bridges, implant abutments, frameworks and dentures in dental CAD software from an intraoral or model scan: setting margins, insertion path, contacts and occlusion, and sending the design to mill or print. A person who has it designs a restoration that seats and meets the bite with little adjustment.
skills.learned: On the job in a digital dental laboratory; software makers' courses. Digital Workflow is a specialty of the National Board for Certification in Dental Laboratory Technology's Certified Dental Technician credential.

skills.name: Dental Milling and Sintering
skills.what: Making restorations from a design on a dental mill: nesting the parts in a zirconia, wax, PMMA, glass-ceramic or metal blank, running the mill, separating and finishing the parts and sintering or crystallizing them in the furnace's program. A person who has it keeps tools and calibration in order so parts come off the mill fitting the design.
skills.learned: On the job in a digital dental laboratory; mill makers train users.

skills.name: Denture Fabrication
skills.what: Making complete and partial dentures: building baseplates and bite rims, setting teeth to the bite, waxing and processing the acrylic base by heat cure, injection or printing, then finishing and polishing. A person who has it sets up teeth that are stable in the bite and processes a base without porosity or distortion.
skills.learned: Dental laboratory technology programs; on the job. Complete and partial dentures are specialties of the Certified Dental Technician credential.

skills.name: Dental Ceramics Layering
skills.what: Building up, staining and glazing porcelain on a framework or a full-contour crown to the shade, translucency and shape of natural teeth, firing it through the furnace's programs. A person who has it matches the shade, keeps the anatomy and leaves contacts and bite that need no adjustment.
skills.learned: Years at the bench under a ceramist; dental laboratory technology programs. Ceramics is a specialty of the Certified Dental Technician credential.

skills.name: Lens Power Verification
skills.what: Checking a finished lens or pair against the prescription: sphere, cylinder, axis, prism, add and optical centers on a lensmeter, thickness and base curve, and a cosmetic inspection under light, to the ANSI Z80.1 tolerances. A person who has it passes or rejects a job on measurement and records why.
skills.learned: On the job in an optical laboratory; covered in optician training.

skills.name: Lens Coating
skills.what: Coating ophthalmic lenses: cleaning them to coating standard, applying hard coat by dip or spin, and building antireflective and mirror stacks in a vacuum box coater, then checking adhesion, color and reflection. A person who has it keeps the coating room clean, runs the coater's recipes and can tell a coating defect from a surfacing one.
skills.learned: On the job in an optical laboratory's coating department.

skills.name: Lens Edging and Mounting
skills.what: Shaping a finished lens to its frame and mounting it: tracing the frame, laying out the optical center and axis, edging with the right bevel or groove, drilling for rimless mounts, and fitting and aligning the lenses in the frame. A person who has it delivers a pair that sits stress-free in the frame with centers and axis where the prescription puts them.
skills.learned: On the job in an optical laboratory or optical shop.

skills.name: Lens Surfacing
skills.what: Cutting a prescription into a semi-finished lens blank: blocking the blank, generating the curves on a CNC generator, polishing (and fining where needed), deblocking and cleaning. A person who has it sets up each job from the lab's software, keeps tools and laps current and makes a lens that meets the prescription and is free of cosmetic flaws.
skills.learned: On the job in an optical laboratory; some community colleges offer an ophthalmic laboratory technician certificate.

skills.name: Jewelry Fabrication
skills.what: Making and repairing jewelry at the bench: sawing, filing, forming and torch soldering precious metal, sizing rings, assembling findings and chain, and cleaning up castings for setting and polishing. A person who has it solders without porosity or fire scale, sizes a ring without distorting it and works in gold, platinum and silver.
skills.learned: Bench jewelry programs and apprenticeships; on the job. Jewelers of America certifies bench jewelers.

skills.name: Stone Setting
skills.what: Setting gemstones in metal: prong, bezel, channel, pave and flush settings, cutting seats with burs and gravers and securing each stone so it is level, tight and undamaged. A person who has it sets a stone straight and secure under magnification and can reset or replace one.
skills.learned: Bench jewelry programs and years at the bench; Jewelers of America's bench certification tests setting.

skills.name: Catheter Reflow and Tipping
skills.what: Forming catheter shafts and ends with heat: laminating jackets over a liner, braid or coil on a mandrel under heat-shrink (reflow), bonding tubing sections, and forming soft tips, flares and necks in heated dies. A person who has it sets temperature, dwell and speed for each material, removes the heat-shrink and mandrel without damage and checks the joint, outer diameter and tip.
skills.learned: On the job at a catheter maker.

skills.name: Microscope Assembly
skills.what: Assembling and inspecting parts too small to work by eye, under a stereo microscope: handling with tweezers and vacuum pick-ups, placing, crimping, bonding and inspecting at magnification. A person who has it works for hours at the scope without damaging or losing a part.
skills.learned: On the job in medical device, hearing aid and microelectronics plants; assemblers are qualified station by station.

skills.name: UV Adhesive Bonding
skills.what: Bonding small plastic, metal and glass parts with light-curing adhesive: preparing the surfaces, dispensing a measured dot or bead, positioning the parts and curing with UV or visible light at a set intensity and time. A person who has it makes bonds that pass pull testing, keeps adhesive off where it does not belong and checks lamp intensity before each run.
skills.learned: On the job in medical device and electronics assembly; adhesive and equipment suppliers train operators.
tools: UV and LED spot and flood curing systems

skills.name: Bolted Flange Joint Assembly
skills.what: Making up a bolted flanged joint that seals: checking the faces, fitting the gasket, lubricating the studs and tightening them in the pattern and passes the procedure calls for, to a torque or a bolt load. A person who has it aligns the flanges without forcing them, uses calibrated tools and records the joint.
skills.learned: Pipefitter and millwright apprenticeships; the training and qualification of bolted joint assembly personnel in ASME PCC-1, Appendix A.

skills.name: Hand Tool Woodworking
skills.what: Shaping and fitting wood with hand tools: marking out, sawing, chiseling, planing, scraping and filing. A person who has it fits a joint, a door or a drawer by hand where a machine cannot, and keeps edge tools sharp.
skills.learned: Woodworking and cabinetmaking programs, and the first year of a cabinetmaking apprenticeship.

skills.name: Cabinet Hardware Installation
skills.what: Boring for and fitting hinges, drawer slides, shelf supports, locks and pulls, and adjusting doors and drawers so the reveals are even. A person who has it sets up boring jigs and machines for each make of hardware, and adjusts the finished cabinet to close true.
skills.learned: On the job; hardware makers train installers.

skills.name: Casework Assembly
skills.what: Assembling cabinet boxes, face frames, drawers and doors from machined parts, gluing, fastening and squaring them in case clamps and jigs. A person who has it builds a box square and flat to the shop drawing, and catches a wrong or damaged part before it is built in.
skills.learned: On the job in a cabinet plant; cabinetmaking apprenticeships.
tools: Pneumatic nailers, staplers and screw guns

skills.name: Veneer and Laminate Application
skills.what: Bonding wood veneer and high-pressure laminate to panels and countertops: cutting and matching sheets, spreading adhesive, pressing in a vacuum, cold or hot press, and trimming the edges. A person who has it lays out veneer matches, keeps the bond free of bubbles and telegraphing, and trims flush without chipping.
skills.learned: On the job in a millwork or furniture shop; architectural woodwork and cabinetmaking programs.

skills.name: Wood Joinery
skills.what: Cutting and assembling the joints that hold wood together (dados, rabbets, mortise and tenon, dowels, biscuits and dovetails, by machine or by hand) and gluing and clamping them. A person who has it chooses the joint for the load and the wood's movement, and makes it tight and square.
skills.learned: Cabinetmaking and furniture programs and apprenticeships.

skills.name: Bent Lamination and Curved Work
skills.what: Making curved parts by gluing thin plies over a form or by steam bending solid wood, and building curved casework and millwork from them. A person who has it builds the form, allows for springback, and gets a curve that holds its shape and matches its neighbor.
skills.learned: Years in a millwork or furniture shop; cabinetmaking and furniture programs.

skills.name: Truss Component Sawing
skills.what: Cutting lumber for trusses and wall panels on automated component and linear saws from the design's cut list: angles, lengths and bevels, by species and grade. A person who has it loads the cut file, checks the first piece of each setup, and labels and stages members for the tables.
skills.learned: On the job in a truss plant.

skills.name: Truss Jig Setup
skills.what: Setting the stops and jigs on a truss assembly table to the truss drawing, by hand or with an automated jigging system and laser projector. A person who has it lays out the heel, peak and panel points accurately, so every truss on the setup comes out the same.
skills.learned: On the job in a truss plant.

skills.name: Truss Plating and Pressing
skills.what: Placing a metal connector plate at each joint to the truss drawing, and pressing it fully into the wood with a gantry or roller press. A person who has it places each plate within tolerance, keeps joints tight, and checks plate embedment and lumber grade as the in-plant quality rules ask.
skills.learned: On the job in a truss plant; the Structural Building Components Association's in-plant quality training.

skills.name: Wall Panel Framing
skills.what: Building wall panels in a plant: laying out plates, studs, headers and openings from the panel drawing, nailing on framing tables or a framing line, and sheathing and squaring the panel. A person who has it builds each panel to the drawing's openings and dimensions, so it stands plumb on site.
skills.learned: On the job in a component plant; carpentry programs.

skills.name: Cabinet and Interior Installation
skills.what: Setting the cabinets, countertops, furniture, ceilings, wall panels and trim inside an RV or a factory-built home: fitting them to the walls and slide-outs, fastening into the framing and leaving doors and drawers square and working. A person who has it hides fasteners and joints and protects the finish already in place.
skills.learned: On the job at RV and modular building plants; finish carpentry and cabinetmaking programs.

skills.name: LP Gas System Installation
skills.what: Piping and testing the propane system of an RV or a factory-built home: running the gas line, fitting the regulator and manifold, connecting furnace, water heater and range, and proving the system leak-free by the pressure tests before and after the appliances are connected. A person who has it finds and fixes a leak with a manometer and leak solution, never a flame.
skills.learned: On the job in RV plants, to NFPA 1192 and the RV Industry Association's standards program; in Texas the Railroad Commission licenses LP-gas work on recreational vehicles (Category M).
tools: Black iron, copper and flexible gas line

skills.name: Potable Water and Drain Plumbing
skills.what: Installing the fresh water, waste and vent systems of an RV, a boat or a factory-built home: cutting and crimping or expanding PEX, solvent-welding drain lines, fitting tanks, pump, water heater and fixtures, and testing water and drain for leaks. A person who has it routes lines clear of heat and chafe and leaves the system able to drain for winter.
skills.learned: On the job at RV, boat and modular building plants; plumbing apprenticeships.

skills.name: Roof Membrane Installation
skills.what: Covering a roof with a single-ply membrane (TPO, EPDM or PVC) or a one-piece fiberglass or aluminum skin: rolling and adhering it, cutting around vents and fixtures, and sealing every edge and penetration. A person who has it leaves no wrinkle or dry spot and lays the lap sealant so water runs off.
skills.learned: On the job in the roof department of an RV plant.

skills.name: Wall and Roof Panel Lamination
skills.what: Building the sidewalls, roof and floor of an RV or a modular building as bonded panels: laying the skin, frame, foam and backer on the table, spreading adhesive, and pressing them in a vacuum or pinch-roll laminator through the cure. A person who has it keeps the stack square and within the adhesive's open time and checks the panel for voids and delamination.
skills.learned: On the job in the lamination department of an RV or modular building plant.

skills.name: Fabric Spreading
skills.what: Laying fabric from the roll into a lay of many plies on the cutting table, by hand or with a spreading machine, at the length, ply count and tension the marker calls for. A person who has it keeps edges aligned and plies flat and unstretched, matches stripes and plaids, splices in the right places and flags defects so they are cut out.
skills.learned: On the job in a cutting room.

skills.name: Tech Pack Reading
skills.what: Reading the specification of a sewn product: the flat sketch, bill of materials, measurement chart and its tolerances, stitch and seam types, and the construction and label notes. A person who has it can tell from the tech pack what is to be cut and sewn, in what order, and what the finished piece must measure.
skills.learned: On the job; apparel and sewn products programs teach it in the first term.

skills.name: Fabric Cutting
skills.what: Cutting a lay of fabric, or single plies of upholstery goods, into the pieces of a product by straight knife, band knife or die press, or on a computer-controlled cutter run from the marker file, then notching, drilling and bundling the pieces with their tickets. A person who has it cuts to the line on every ply, matches stripes, plaids and nap where the order calls for it, keeps blades and the cutting surface in condition and sends complete, correctly ticketed bundles to the sewing floor.
skills.learned: On the job in a cutting room of an apparel, sewn-products, upholstery or seating plant; cutter makers train operators on automated cutters.

skills.name: Garment Construction
skills.what: Sewing a complete garment or other sewn product from cut pieces to finished item, on whatever machines it needs and in the right order of operations, from the pattern and the tech pack. A person who has it builds first samples and prototypes, works out how a new style should be sewn and shows production sewers the method.
skills.learned: Apparel and sewn products programs; on the job as a sample sewer after years of production sewing.

skills.name: Foam and Padding Application
skills.what: Cutting, gluing and wrapping foam, fiber and padding on frames and in cushions to the comfort and shape specified. A person who has it builds a cushion that fills its cover, crowns evenly and recovers after use.
skills.learned: On the job in an upholstered furniture plant.

skills.name: Spring Installation
skills.what: Installing the spring system of upholstered seating: sinuous springs and clips, coil units and webbing, and coils hand-tied eight ways. A person who has it sets the springs to the right arc and tension so the seat sits level and does not squeak.
skills.learned: On the job in an upholstered furniture plant; hand tying is learned from an experienced upholsterer.

skills.name: Upholstery Covering
skills.what: Fitting, pulling and stapling the cover onto a padded frame: aligning seams and patterns, pulling evenly, and finishing corners, welts and dust covers. A person who has it covers a piece smooth and square, with stripes and seams where they belong.
skills.learned: On the job in an upholstered furniture plant; upholstery courses at some community colleges and trade schools.

skills.name: Tufting and Channeling
skills.what: Making tufted and channeled upholstery: laying out the diamond or channel pattern, folding the cover into pleats, and fixing buttons or channels through the padding. A person who has it keeps the pattern even across the whole piece.
skills.learned: Years of upholstery practice, in custom and high-end furniture shops.

skills.name: Leather Cutting
skills.what: Cutting leather into the parts of shoes, boots, bags and belts: reading each hide for grade, flaws, stretch and direction, and cutting by hand knife, by die on a clicking press or on a computer-controlled cutter that nests the parts to the hide. A person who has it gets the most good parts from a hide, each from the right area and in the right direction.
skills.learned: On the job in a footwear or leather goods plant; cutters are among the longest-trained people on the floor.
tools: CNC leather cutters with hide scanning

skills.name: Shoe Bottoming
skills.what: Attaching the bottom of a shoe or boot: welting and outsole stitching for Goodyear welt and stitchdown construction, or roughing, cementing and pressing for cemented construction, then trimming, heeling and finishing the sole edge. A person who has it builds a bottom that is square, sound and bonded or stitched all round.
skills.learned: On the job in a footwear plant.

skills.name: Shoe Lasting
skills.what: Shaping a stitched upper over the last: inserting counter and toe box, pulling the upper over at the toe, sides and heel by lasting machine or by hand, and fixing it to the insole with cement, tacks or staples. A person who has it lasts an upper smooth and centered, with no wrinkles and a straight vamp.
skills.learned: On the job in a footwear plant.
tools: Toe, side and heel-seat lasting machines

skills.name: PCB Rework and Repair
skills.what: Removing and replacing components on a built circuit board and repairing the board itself: jumper wires, cut and rejoined traces, lifted pads, and conformal coating taken off and touched up. A person who has it picks the approved method for the part and the damage, protects the parts around it and leaves work that passes inspection to the class the product is built to.
skills.learned: An IPC-7711/7721 course from an IPC-licensed training center, ending in the Certified IPC Specialist credential, renewed every two years; built on hand soldering experience.
tools: Jumper wire and trace repair kits

skills.name: Bare Board Electrical Test
skills.what: Testing every net of a bare board for opens and shorts on a flying-probe or fixture tester before it ships: loading the netlist, setting the resistance thresholds, running the panels and marking or repairing what fails. A person who has it tells a real defect from a contact problem.
skills.learned: On the job at a printed circuit board fabricator; IPC-9252 sets the requirements for electrical test of unpopulated boards.

skills.name: PCB Drilling and Routing
skills.what: Drilling and routing panels on CNC machines: through, blind and back-drilled holes to the program, then routing the boards out of the panel. A person who has it sets up the stacks with entry and backup material, changes bits by hit count and checks hole size, position and depth.
skills.learned: On the job at a printed circuit board fabricator.

skills.name: PCB Imaging
skills.what: Transferring a circuit board's pattern: laminating dry-film photoresist onto copper panels, exposing it through a phototool or by laser direct imaging, and developing it; and imaging the solder mask the same way. A person who has it registers each layer to the drill, controls exposure energy and keeps the yellow room clean.
skills.learned: On the job at a printed circuit board fabricator.
tools: Contact exposure units and laser direct imagers

skills.name: PCB Multilayer Lamination
skills.what: Building a multilayer board: treating the inner layers for bond, stacking cores and prepreg with copper foil on pins to the stack-up, and pressing the book through its cure cycle. A person who has it holds registration and thickness and reads a press cycle that went wrong.
skills.learned: On the job at a printed circuit board fabricator.
tools: Thickness gauges and X-ray target drills

skills.name: Shipboard Cable Installation
skills.what: Pulling and securing power, control and signal cable through a ship: routing it in the cableways the cable routing drawings show, walking it in by hand, keeping its bend radius and separation, and banding it to the hangers. A person who has it leaves each end long enough to terminate and tags every cable.
skills.learned: Electrician apprenticeships at the shipyards and on the job; warship work follows the Navy's installation standard, MIL-STD-2003.

skills.name: Cable Penetration Sealing
skills.what: Taking cable through decks and watertight or fire-rated bulkheads: laying out and fitting stuffing tubes and multi-cable transits, packing them to the specification and proving the seal. A person who has it keeps every watertight and fire boundary whole around the cables that cross it.
skills.learned: On the job at shipyards and offshore fabricators; the transit makers train and certify installers.

skills.name: Low-Voltage DC Wiring
skills.what: Wiring the 12- and 24-volt DC systems of boats, RVs and specialty vehicles: batteries and switches, distribution panels, chargers, converters and inverters, and the circuits they feed. A person who has it sizes wire for current and voltage drop, fuses each circuit at its source, makes sealed terminations and checks the system with a meter.
skills.learned: On the job at boat and RV plants; the American Boat and Yacht Council's marine electrical certification; RV technician courses.

skills.name: Core and Coil Assembly
skills.what: Putting the coils on the core legs, restacking the top yoke, fitting the clamping frames, insulation and supports, and connecting the leads to the bushings and tap changer by brazing, crimping or bolting. A person who has it presses the assembly to height and checks electrical clearances before it is dried.
skills.learned: On the job at a transformer plant.
tools: Brazing and crimping tools for leads

skills.name: Transformer Coil Winding
skills.what: Winding the coils of a distribution or power transformer: layer, disc, helical or foil windings of copper or aluminum, with the paper and pressboard insulation, cooling ducts and taps placed as the winding sheet calls for. A person who has it keeps the coil tight, square and to dimension and checks turns and resistance as it goes.
skills.learned: On the job at a transformer plant; the makers speak of years of practice for power-class coils.

skills.name: Transformer Core Stacking
skills.what: Building a transformer core from grain-oriented electrical steel: laying the cut laminations in the step-lap pattern on the stacking table, holding the joint gaps and keeping the steel clean and unbent, then clamping legs and yokes, or forming and annealing a wound core. A person who has it builds a core whose losses and noise meet the design.
skills.learned: On the job at a transformer plant.

skills.name: Transformer Processing and Oil Filling
skills.what: Drying a core and coil assembly in a vapor-phase or vacuum oven, setting it in its tank, sealing and pressure-testing the tank, and filling it with insulating fluid under vacuum. A person who has it follows the drying curve to the moisture limit and tests the fluid's dielectric strength and water content before release.
skills.learned: On the job at a transformer plant.
tools: Vacuum pumps and oil processing rigs
Dielectric strength and moisture test sets

skills.name: Transformer Electrical Testing
skills.what: Running a transformer's routine tests: turns ratio and polarity, winding resistance, no-load and load losses, insulation resistance and power factor, applied and induced potential, and lightning impulse on power units, against the limits of IEEE C57.12. A person who has it sets the test up safely, reads a failed result and says what in the unit caused it.
skills.learned: On the job in a transformer plant's test bay or with an electrical testing company; the InterNational Electrical Testing Association certifies test technicians.
tools: Loss measurement systems and impulse generators

skills.name: Optics Cleaning and Handling
skills.what: Handling and cleaning lenses, mirrors, windows and fiber ends without scratching or contaminating them: the right gloves and tools, drag-wipe and solvent methods, and inspection of the surface under light against a scratch-dig specification. A person who has it knows which coatings and materials each method would harm.
skills.learned: On the job; the first courses of optics and photonics technician programs (Monroe Community College, Front Range Community College).
tools: Lens tissue, swabs and reagent-grade solvents

skills.name: Optical Alignment
skills.what: Aligning lenses, mirrors, prisms and sources in an optical assembly: centering and spacing the elements, collimating and focusing with an autocollimator, an alignment telescope or a laser, and locking the alignment so it holds through test. A person who has it reads the optical drawing's tolerances and knows which adjustment moves which error.
skills.learned: Optics and photonics technician programs; on the job.

skills.name: Optical Cementing and Bonding
skills.what: Joining optics: cementing lens doublets and bonding lenses, prisms and windows into their mounts with UV-cured and two-part adhesives, holding the alignment while the adhesive cures. A person who has it dispenses the right amount, with no voids and nothing on the clear aperture.
skills.learned: On the job at optics and electro-optics makers; optics technician programs.

skills.name: Optical Polishing
skills.what: Grinding and polishing glass, crystal and ceramic optics to curve, figure and finish: generating, fine grinding, and pitch, pad or computer-controlled polishing, checking radius, figure and centering as the work goes. A person who has it brings a surface to its specification without sleeks, scratches or turned edges.
skills.learned: Optical fabrication courses (Monroe Community College's Optical Systems Technology degree, Front Range's optics fabrication) and on the job in optics shops.

skills.name: Interferometric Optical Testing
skills.what: Measuring an optic's surface figure or an assembly's wavefront with an interferometer, and its image quality on an MTF bench: setting up the reference, nulling the fringes and reading power, irregularity and aberrations against the drawing. A person who has it knows when the setup, and not the part, is the error.
skills.learned: Optics and photonics technician programs (metrology courses); on the job.

skills.name: Equipment Commissioning
skills.what: Bringing new, moved or changed equipment into production: setting and leveling it where it stands, checking it against its drawings, proving every input, output, interlock and safety circuit, powering it up, running it dry and then with product, running the factory and site acceptance tests, and teaching the operators to run it. A person who has it works from a checklist rather than memory and hands the machine over making good parts, with its faults closed and its documents current.
skills.learned: On the job, on a first installation beside an integrator, a machine builder's service engineer or an experienced engineer; machine builders and integrators train their own people.
tools: Factory and site acceptance test procedures
Laptop with the controller's and drives' software

skills.name: Food Safety Plan Development
skills.what: Writing and keeping a food plant's food safety plan: the hazard analysis of every ingredient and step; the critical control points and preventive controls with their limits, monitoring, corrective actions and verification; the validation behind each kill step; and the reanalysis whenever anything changes. A person who has it can take an auditor or inspector through the plan and the records that prove it works.
skills.learned: HACCP courses accredited by the International HACCP Alliance; the Food Safety Preventive Controls Alliance course that qualifies a Preventive Controls Qualified Individual under FDA rules; years in quality at a food plant.

skills.name: Cleaning Validation
skills.what: Proving that a cleaning procedure removes what it must (product, allergen residue, cleaning agent and microbes) to a set or calculated limit: choosing the worst-case products and surfaces, swab and rinse sampling with recovery studies, testing, and writing the protocol and report into the procedure. A person who has it calculates carryover limits, samples the hardest-to-clean spots so the result means something, and knows what must be revalidated when the equipment or the product changes.
skills.learned: On the job in a food or pharmaceutical quality, validation or sanitation group, with short courses on FDA and international guidance.
tools: Allergen test kits and ATP swabs

skills.name: Thermal Validation
skills.what: Mapping and proving the temperatures of sterilizers, depyrogenation ovens, freezers, incubators, warehouses and steam-in-place systems with calibrated thermocouples and data loggers: empty-chamber distribution, loaded heat penetration and biological indicator challenges. A person who has it places probes at the hot and cold spots, calibrates them before and after, works out lethality for a sterilization cycle and states whether the unit passes.
skills.learned: On the job in validation groups, with training from the makers of validation loggers.

skills.name: Industrial Frying
skills.what: Frying snacks, doughnuts and prepared foods in continuous or batch fryers: holding oil temperature and dwell time, filtering and topping up the oil and testing its quality, and keeping the fire suppression system ready. A person who has it holds colour, moisture and oil content to target and knows when the oil must be changed.
skills.learned: On the job at a snack, bakery or prepared-food plant.
tools: Heat exchangers and thermal fluid systems

skills.name: Food Extrusion Cooking
skills.what: Cooking and shaping cereal, snack, pet food and feed doughs in an extruder: setting feed rate, water and steam, screw speed and barrel temperatures, changing dies and cutters, and holding the product's density and size. A person who has it starts and stops the extruder without plugging it and brings bulk density back when the raw material changes.
skills.learned: On the job at a cereal, snack or pet food plant; extrusion short courses at Texas A&M and Washington State University and from extruder makers.

skills.name: Food Forming and Depositing
skills.what: Shaping food on the line: forming patties, nuggets and shaped products from ground or chopped meat and vegetables, and depositing batters, fillings, sauces and confectionery into pans and moulds or onto product. A person who has it sets the former or depositor for weight and shape, keeps pieces on weight through the run, and clears and cleans the heads safely.
skills.learned: On the job at a meat, bakery, confectionery or prepared-food plant.

skills.name: Chocolate Tempering and Enrobing
skills.what: Working chocolate and compound coatings on the confectionery line: tempering chocolate so it sets glossy and snaps, coating centres in the enrober and setting them in the cooling tunnel, and moulding solid pieces. A person who has it checks temper with a temper meter, holds coating weight to target and fixes bloom, streaks and tails.
skills.learned: On the job at a confectionery plant; chocolate and confectionery equipment makers' and associations' short courses.

skills.name: Knife Sharpening and Steeling
skills.what: Keeping a boning or trimming knife's edge through a shift: steeling it every few cuts, sharpening it on stones or a sharpening machine when the steel no longer brings it back, and handling, carrying and storing it safely. A person who has it cuts all shift without forcing the knife, which protects their hands and wrists and keeps the yield.
skills.learned: On the job in the first weeks at a meat, poultry or seafood plant, from a knife trainer; part of every community-college and extension meat cutting certificate.

skills.name: Carcass Antimicrobial Intervention
skills.what: Running the steps that cut bacteria on carcasses and parts: hot water and steam pasteurization cabinets, and lactic or peracetic acid sprays and dips. A person who has it sets and verifies concentration, temperature, pressure and coverage on the schedule the plant's HACCP plan names, records each check and stops product when one fails.
skills.learned: On the job at a meat or poultry plant, usually as the intervention or food safety technician.

skills.name: Carcass Dressing
skills.what: Turning a stunned animal into a clean dressed carcass on the harvest line: sticking and bleeding, removing the hide or feathers, the head and shanks, eviscerating without spilling the gut, splitting with the carcass saw, and trimming visible contamination before the final wash. A person who has it makes their station's cut at line speed and keeps fecal material, ingesta and milk off the carcass, which USDA holds to zero tolerance.
skills.learned: On the job at a slaughter plant, station by station; covered in community-college and extension meat processing certificates.

skills.name: Carcass Fabrication
skills.what: Breaking chilled beef, pork or lamb carcasses into primals and subprimals on the fabrication floor: following the seams and bones, cutting to the specification the customer orders and sawing bone-in cuts. A person who has it makes their station's cut at line speed and knows from the cut sheet what each piece must be.
skills.learned: On the job on a plant's fabrication floor; community-college and extension meat cutting certificates teach carcass breakdown into primal, subprimal and retail cuts.

skills.name: Humane Handling and Stunning
skills.what: Moving livestock or birds to slaughter calmly and making each one insensible before it is bled, as the Humane Methods of Slaughter Act requires: driving animals quietly, stunning with a captive bolt, electricity or carbon dioxide, checking each for insensibility and stunning again at once when one is not. A person who has it stuns on the first attempt and keeps the stunner and the records the inspector reviews.
skills.learned: On the job under the plant's written humane handling program, with stunner training and audits to the Meat Institute's animal handling guidelines; USDA FSIS inspectors verify it daily.
tools: Pneumatic and cartridge captive bolt stunners
Electrical and carbon dioxide stunning systems

skills.name: Meat Deboning and Trimming
skills.what: Taking the bone out of meat, poultry and fish and trimming fat, gristle and defects to the specification: lean points, fat cover, no bone fragments. A person who has it bones a cut clean with little meat left on the bone, trims to spec without over-trimming, and works a powered trimmer as well as a knife.
skills.learned: On the job at a meat, poultry or seafood plant, under a knife trainer.

skills.name: Smokehouse Cooking and Chilling
skills.what: Cooking, smoking and then chilling processed meat and poultry (hot dogs, hams, bacon, deli logs) in batch or continuous smokehouses and ovens. A person who has it loads to the pattern, runs the cook schedule until the product reaches its lethality temperature, chills it within the stabilization limits and records the internal temperatures USDA requires.
skills.learned: On the job at a meat processing plant; university extension and meat science short courses teach FSIS's cooking and stabilization guidelines.

skills.name: Dough Fermentation and Proofing
skills.what: Controlling the yeast in a dough from the mixer to the oven: sponges, liquid ferments and floor time, then the proofer's temperature and humidity. A person who has it judges when a dough or a pan is ready, adjusts time and conditions to the room and the flour, and keeps the line from waiting on underproofed or overproofed product.
skills.learned: On the job at a commercial bakery; AIB International's baking science courses.

skills.name: Dough Makeup
skills.what: Turning bulk dough into pieces ready to proof on the make-up line: dividing to weight, rounding, intermediate proof, moulding or sheeting and laminating, and panning or cutting. A person who has it sets the divider to scale weight, adjusts the moulder and sheeter for shape, and keeps the line fed and running.
skills.learned: On the job at a commercial bakery.

skills.name: Dough Mixing
skills.what: Mixing bread and bun dough to full development at the right temperature: metering flour, water and minor ingredients, setting the water temperature so the dough comes off at its target, mixing for the time and energy the product needs, and judging development by touch and a window test. A person who has it brings each batch off the mixer at the same temperature and consistency and changes the water when the flour changes.
skills.learned: On the job at a commercial bakery; AIB International's baking courses and community-college baking programs.

skills.name: Industrial Oven Baking
skills.what: Baking at production scale in tunnel, rack and spiral ovens: setting each zone's temperature, the steam and the belt speed to the bake profile, checking colour, volume and internal temperature, and cooling the product before slicing. A person who has it holds the bake through a shift as the load changes and finds out why a bake has gone wrong.
skills.learned: On the job at a commercial bakery; AIB International's courses and oven makers' training.

skills.name: Cheesemaking
skills.what: Making cheese in the vat to the make sheet: ripening the milk with culture, setting it with rennet, cutting the curd, cooking and stirring it, draining the whey, then cheddaring, milling, salting, moulding and pressing it. A person who has it times each step by acidity, temperature and the feel of the curd, and corrects the make when the milk changes.
skills.learned: On the job under a licensed cheesemaker. Wisconsin licenses cheesemakers: 18 months as a cheesemaker assistant, approved courses and a state exam. The Center for Dairy Research at UW-Madison runs the courses.

skills.name: Milk Separation and Standardization
skills.what: Separating raw milk into cream and skim and recombining them to the fat, and for cheese the protein, the product calls for, after receiving and sampling the milk off the truck. A person who has it runs the separator and in-line standardizing, checks fat by test and adjusts until each batch is on target.
skills.learned: On the job at a dairy or cheese plant. Under the Grade A Pasteurized Milk Ordinance, states license or evaluate the people who sample raw milk.

skills.name: Cheese Ripening and Grading
skills.what: Bringing cheese from the press to sale: brining, waxing or wrapping, holding the aging rooms at their temperature and humidity, turning and caring for the wheels, and grading each lot by plugging it and judging its flavour, body, texture and appearance. A person who has it can tell from a core how a cheese is developing and decide which vats go to which use.
skills.learned: Years in a cheese plant's make room and aging rooms; dairy science short courses on cheese grading; the Wisconsin Master Cheesemaker program.

skills.name: Feed Pelleting
skills.what: Making feed into pellets: grinding and batching the formula, conditioning the mash with steam, running the pellet mill through the right die, then cooling, crumbling and screening the pellets. A person who has it holds conditioning temperature and pellet durability, changes dies and rolls, and keeps the mill from plugging.
skills.learned: On the job at a feed mill; feed manufacturing short courses at Kansas State University and from feed industry associations.

skills.name: Flour Milling
skills.what: Running a flour, corn or rice mill: cleaning the grain and tempering it to moisture, setting the break and reduction roller mills, sifters and purifiers to the flow sheet, and adjusting the mill on the flour's ash, moisture, protein and extraction. A person who has it walks the mill, reads the stocks by hand and eye, and keeps it running without chokes.
skills.learned: On the job under a head miller; the International Association of Operative Millers' courses with Kansas State University, and IAOM's online milling technician certificate with Cowley College.

skills.name: Barrel Aging
skills.what: Aging wine or spirit in oak: preparing, filling and bunging barrels, topping and stirring wine and racking it off its lees, sampling, and dumping aged spirit, along with cleaning, storing, rotating and recording the barrels. A person who has it moves barrels safely, keeps them full and sound, and knows each barrel's contents and history.
skills.learned: On the job in a winery's barrel room or a distillery's warehouse; enology and distilling programs.

skills.name: Beverage Clarification and Filtration
skills.what: Making beer, wine or spirit bright and stable before it is packaged: settling and fining, centrifuging, filtering through diatomaceous earth, sheets, crossflow membranes or cartridges, and sterile filtering at bottling. A person who has it sets up and runs each filter without picking up oxygen or contamination, watches pressure and haze, and knows when a filter is spent.
skills.learned: On the job in a brewery, winery or distillery; brewing and enology programs.

skills.name: Beverage Fermentation
skills.what: Turning wort, mash or juice into beer, spirit wash or wine with yeast: propagating and pitching it at the right rate, controlling fermentation temperature, following gravity or sugar to the end, and harvesting and re-pitching the yeast after checking its viability. A person who has it keeps fermentations on schedule and clean, and catches a stuck or infected one in time to act.
skills.learned: On the job in a brewery, winery or distillery; the Chartered Institute of Brewers and Distillers' General Certificates; university brewing, enology and distilling programs.

skills.name: Grain Mashing
skills.what: Turning grain into a fermentable wort or mash in a brewhouse or a distillery's cook. The grain is milled, then mashed at the recipe's rest temperatures (or, in a distillery, corn is cooked with enzymes) until the starch converts. For beer the wort is lautered off the grain, boiled with hops, whirlpooled and cooled to the fermenter. A person who has it hits the brew's temperatures, volumes and gravity, and knows what went wrong when conversion or run-off is slow.
skills.learned: On the job in a brewery or distillery; the Chartered Institute of Brewers and Distillers' General Certificates in Brewing and in Distilling; university brewing and distilling certificates.

skills.name: Grape Crushing and Pressing
skills.what: Bringing grapes into the winery at harvest: receiving and sampling the fruit, sorting, destemming and crushing it, and making additions. Whites are pressed at once and reds after fermentation, with the press fractions cut apart. A person who has it keeps the crush pad moving through the harvest day and sends each lot to the right tank with its records.
skills.learned: On the job as a harvest cellar worker; community-college and university viticulture and enology programs.

skills.name: Spirits Distillation
skills.what: Distilling a fermented wash into spirit. Pot stills run in batches, with the cuts between heads, hearts and tails made by proof, temperature, taste and smell; a column and doubler run continuously to a target proof. The spirit is then reduced to proof and what was made is gauged for the federal records. A person who has it brings every run off with the same character and proof, and keeps the still safe around high-proof alcohol.
skills.learned: On the job under a head distiller; the Chartered Institute of Brewers and Distillers' General Certificate in Distilling; university distilling certificates. Gauging and records follow the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau's rules.

skills.name: Wine and Spirits Blending
skills.what: Putting lots of wine or aged spirit together into a product that tastes the same every release: tasting and analysing the components, making bench blends, choosing one, and scaling it up in tank with its additions and records. A person who has it can hold a house style across vintages or warehouses and say what part each component plays.
skills.learned: Years as a cellar master, winemaker or distiller; enology and distilling degree programs.

skills.name: Steam-in-Place Operation
skills.what: Sterilizing vessels, transfer lines and filters where they stand with pure steam: venting air, holding every drain point at temperature for the cycle time, and cooling under sterile air without pulling a vacuum. A person who has it runs the cycle, confirms every cold point met temperature and keeps the system sterile until it is used.
skills.learned: On the job in biotech and sterile drug plants.

skills.name: Radiation Sterilization
skills.what: Sterilizing medical devices and components with gamma rays, an electron beam or X-rays: loading product to the validated pattern, placing dosimeters, running the irradiator and reviewing the dose record before release. A person who has it knows why a load's density and position change its dose and works inside the plant's radiation safety rules.
skills.learned: On the job at a contract or in-house sterilization plant; the process is validated to ISO 11137.

skills.name: Form-Fill-Seal Bagging
skills.what: Running the machines that make a bag from film, fill it and seal it, with the multihead weigher that portions the product: threading and registering the film, setting jaw temperatures, pressures and times, changing formers for a new bag size, and checking seals and weights. A person who has it keeps the bagger making sealed, on-weight bags and finds why a seal leaks.
skills.learned: On the job at a snack, frozen food, coffee or produce plant; machine makers' operator courses; PMMI's mechatronics certificates for packaging technicians.

skills.name: Vacuum and Modified Atmosphere Packaging
skills.what: Packing meat, poultry, cheese and fresh food in film with the air drawn out or replaced by a gas mix: running thermoform-fill-seal machines, vacuum chamber and shrink-bag lines and tray sealers, setting vacuum, gas flush, seal and shrink, and checking seals and residual oxygen. A person who has it changes tooling and film for a new pack and catches a leaking pack before it ships.
skills.learned: On the job at a meat, poultry or cheese plant; packaging machine makers' courses.
tools: Vacuum chamber and rotary bag machines

skills.name: Sterile Barrier Sealing
skills.what: Sealing medical devices into the pouches, trays and lids that keep them sterile: setting the sealer to its validated temperature, pressure and dwell, sealing, and checking each seal for width, channels and wrinkles and by peel and leak tests. A person who has it never releases a seal made outside the validated settings.
skills.learned: On the job at a medical device plant; the requirements for the package and its sealing are in ISO 11607.
tools: Band, rotary and platen heat sealers
Dye penetration and bubble leak test kits

skills.name: Capsule Filling
skills.what: Running a capsule filler that separates empty hard capsules, doses powder, pellets or granules into them by dosator or tamping disc, and closes them. A person who has it sets fill weight, checks weight variation and closure at intervals, and corrects split, dented and under-filled capsules.
skills.learned: On the job under GMP in solid-dose plants.

skills.name: Sterile Filtration and Filter Integrity Testing
skills.what: Passing a drug solution or gas through a sterilizing-grade filter into the sterile zone, and proving the filter was intact before and after use by bubble point, diffusion or pressure-hold test. A person who has it installs and wets the filter correctly, runs the integrity test and knows what to do with the batch when a test fails.
skills.learned: On the job in sterile and biotech manufacturing, with training from filter makers.

skills.name: Visual Inspection of Injectables
skills.what: Inspecting filled vials, syringes and ampoules for visible particles, cracks, fill and closure defects under controlled light, by hand and on semi-automated or automated machines. A person who has it passes the vision screen and the qualification with a seeded defect set, keeps to the inspection time per unit and classifies each reject.
skills.learned: On the job, qualified against a defect set; USP chapters 790 and 1790 set the inspection conditions.
tools: Inspection booths with black and white backgrounds

skills.name: Buffer and Media Preparation
skills.what: Making the buffers and cell culture media a biologics process runs on: weighing components, dissolving them to volume in water for injection, adjusting pH and conductivity, and filtering into bags or tanks. A person who has it follows the batch record exactly, checks pH, conductivity and osmolality against limits, and labels each lot so it can be traced.
skills.learned: Biomanufacturing certificate programs at community colleges, then on the job.

skills.name: Bioreactor Operation
skills.what: Running a stainless or single-use bioreactor or fermenter through a production batch: preparing and sterilizing it, inoculating, holding temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen and feeds, sampling, and harvesting. A person who has it reads the trends, answers an alarm before the culture suffers, and keeps the batch record as each step is done.
skills.learned: Biomanufacturing programs, then on the job.
tools: Sterile sampling systems and tube welders

skills.name: Cell Culture Expansion
skills.what: Growing production cells from a thawed vial up to the volume that seeds the production bioreactor: passaging in flasks, rocking bags and seed bioreactors, counting cells and checking viability. A person who has it works aseptically in a biosafety cabinet, keeps the cells on schedule and spots contamination or poor growth early.
skills.learned: Biomanufacturing programs, then on the job.

skills.name: Tangential Flow Filtration
skills.what: Concentrating a protein and exchanging its buffer by ultrafiltration and diafiltration across membranes, and removing viruses by filtration. A person who has it installs and flushes the membranes, tests their integrity, controls transmembrane pressure and flux, and recovers the product without losing yield.
skills.learned: Biomanufacturing programs, then on the job.

skills.name: Process Chromatography
skills.what: Purifying a protein at production scale on packed columns: packing and testing the column, then equilibrating, loading, washing, eluting and regenerating it on a chromatography skid while collecting the product peak. A person who has it reads the UV, conductivity and pressure traces, cuts the peak at the right point and keeps the resin in condition between cycles.
skills.learned: Biomanufacturing programs, then on the job.

skills.name: Food Chemistry Testing
skills.what: Testing food and beverage samples in the plant lab for what the specification and the product's safety depend on: pH and acidity, moisture and water activity, fat, protein and salt, sugar, alcohol and dissolved gases. A person who has it runs each method to procedure, checks the instrument with a standard first, and reports the result against the limit in time for production to act.
skills.learned: On the job in a food or beverage plant's quality lab; food science and laboratory technology programs.
tools: Moisture balances and water activity meters

skills.name: Food Pathogen Testing
skills.what: Testing food, ingredients and environmental swabs for pathogens such as Listeria, Salmonella and E. coli O157:H7: enriching the sample, screening it by a rapid molecular or immunoassay method, and confirming presumptive positives. A person who has it keeps samples from cross-contaminating, runs the controls with each batch and reports a positive at once.
skills.learned: A microbiology degree or laboratory program, then on the job in a food plant lab or a contract food lab accredited to ISO/IEC 17025.

skills.name: Microbial Identification
skills.what: Naming the organisms found in product, water and environmental samples by Gram stain, biochemical and MALDI-TOF identification, and trending what is found. A person who has it picks colonies cleanly, runs the identification system and reports organisms that point to a contamination source.
skills.learned: Microbiology courses, then on the job.

skills.name: Food Labeling Compliance
skills.what: Making sure what the package says is true and legal: the ingredient statement in order, allergens declared, the nutrition facts calculated or tested, claims allowed, and on the line the right label on the right product. A person who has it checks a label against the formula and the rules and stops a run with the wrong one.
skills.learned: On the job in quality or regulatory work, under FDA's labeling rules (21 CFR Part 101) and, for meat and poultry, USDA FSIS label approval; food science programs.

skills.name: Sensory Evaluation
skills.what: Judging food and beverages by taste, smell, look and texture in a way that can be trusted: checking product against its standard on the line, and running panels by the methods of sensory science (difference tests, descriptive panels, consumer tests). A person who has it tastes without bias, uses the plant's references and scales, and can tell whether a difference is real.
skills.learned: On the job on a plant's or brewery's tasting panel; food science programs and short courses in sensory evaluation.

skills.name: Food Product Formulation
skills.what: Designing or changing a food or beverage formula to a target of taste, texture, cost, nutrition, label and shelf life: choosing ingredients for what they do, making bench samples, and handing the plant a formula and process it can run. A person who has it knows what each ingredient does and can replace one without the consumer noticing.
skills.learned: A food science degree and years in product development; Institute of Food Technologists and Research Chefs Association courses.

skills.name: Shelf-Life Testing
skills.what: Finding out how long a food keeps and stays safe: storing samples at set conditions, including accelerated ones, and testing them on schedule for microbes, rancidity, texture, taste and package integrity, then setting or confirming the date. A person who has it designs the study, keeps the samples and records straight, and can defend the date on the package.
skills.learned: A food science degree, then on the job in product development or quality.

skills.name: Laboratory Information Management System Use
skills.what: Working in the laboratory's information system: logging in samples, entering and reviewing results against specifications, recording instruments and reagents, and releasing results. A person who has it can find any sample's status and history and enters data the way an audit trail expects.
skills.learned: On the job, on the laboratory's own system, in a new analyst's first weeks.

skills.name: Wet Chemical Analysis
skills.what: The chemistry laboratory's bench tests: titrations, pH and conductivity, gravimetric and loss-on-drying results, and density, viscosity and other physical constants of a sample. A person who has it prepares and standardizes reagents, runs the method as written and reports a result a second analyst would repeat.
skills.learned: Chemical technology and chemistry courses at community colleges, then on the job.

skills.name: UV-Visible and Infrared Spectroscopy
skills.what: Identifying materials and measuring concentrations by how they absorb light: FTIR identity tests on raw materials, polymers, adhesives, coatings and contaminants, and UV-visible assays. A person who has it prepares samples by ATR, pellet or solution, checks the instrument's performance, matches the spectrum against a library or reference, and says what the material is and whether it has cured, aged or been contaminated.
skills.learned: Chemistry and materials laboratory courses, then on the instrument at work.

skills.name: Analytical Method Validation
skills.what: Proving that a laboratory test method measures what it claims: specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision, range, robustness and limits of detection and quantitation, to the international guideline for the type of method. A person who has it writes and runs the validation protocol, reports the statistics and transfers the method to another laboratory.
skills.learned: On the job in quality control laboratories, with short courses on the ICH Q2 guideline.

skills.name: Mass Spectrometry
skills.what: Identifying and measuring compounds by their mass with a mass spectrometer coupled to a liquid or gas chromatograph: impurities, residual solvents, extractables and unknowns. A person who has it tunes and calibrates the instrument, builds the acquisition method and interprets the spectra.
skills.learned: Chemistry degree coursework, then on the job.

skills.name: Filtration and Centrifugation
skills.what: Separating solids from liquids in a process: running filter presses, Nutsche filter-dryers, bag and cartridge filters, and decanter and disc-stack centrifuges, then washing and drying the cake. A person who has it sees when a filter is blinded or a centrifuge is out of balance, keeps solvent and dust exposure down and knows the cake is done by its loss on drying.
skills.learned: On the job in chemical, pharmaceutical ingredient and biotech plants; process technology courses.

skills.name: Pigment Dispersion
skills.what: Making paints, inks and coatings: wetting and dispersing pigment into resin and solvent with high-speed dispersers, grinding it fine in bead mills, then letting down, tinting and adjusting the batch to viscosity and color. A person who has it checks grind with a Hegman gauge and viscosity and color against the standard, and adjusts the batch without overshooting.
skills.learned: On the job in paint, ink and coatings plants.

skills.name: Liquid and Semisolid Compounding
skills.what: Making liquids, creams, lotions, gels and ointments to a batch record in jacketed kettles: heating and combining water and oil phases, emulsifying with a homogenizer, drawing vacuum to deaerate, cooling, and adjusting pH and viscosity. A person who has it adds each ingredient at its temperature and step, keeps the emulsion from breaking and samples the batch for release.
skills.learned: On the job under GMP in pharmaceutical, over-the-counter and personal-care plants.

skills.name: Fired Heater Operation
skills.what: Running the gas- and oil-fired process heaters that heat crude and process streams: lighting burners by procedure, holding outlet temperature, controlling draft and excess oxygen, and watching flames and tube temperatures. A person who has it lights off a heater safely, spots flame impingement and hot tubes before a tube fails, and knows what trips a heater and how it is restarted.
skills.learned: Process technology associate degree courses, then training on the unit at a refinery or petrochemical plant.
tools: Tube skin thermocouples and infrared pyrometers

skills.name: Process Compressor Operation
skills.what: Starting, loading and watching the centrifugal and reciprocating compressors that move process gas and hydrogen: lube and seal oil systems, suction drums, recycle and anti-surge control. A person who has it brings a compressor on line without surging or carrying liquid over, reads its vibration and temperatures on rounds and takes it off line when it must.
skills.learned: Process technology courses and training on the unit.

skills.name: Catalytic Unit Operation
skills.what: Running continuous units that convert hydrocarbons over a catalyst: hydrotreaters and hydrocrackers, reformers, fluid catalytic crackers and similar reactors. A person who has it holds reactor temperatures, hydrogen and feed rates within the unit's limits, controls an exotherm, follows catalyst circulation or regeneration, and starts the unit up and down by procedure.
skills.learned: Years on the unit after process technology training.

skills.name: Kraft Pulping
skills.what: Cooking wood chips with white liquor in a batch or continuous digester to free the fiber: feeding chips, setting the liquor-to-wood ratio, temperature and time, and blowing or discharging the cook. A person who has it holds the pulp to its kappa number target, watches chip level and pressure, and knows the safe response to a plugged screen or a hang-up.
skills.learned: On the job through a pulp mill's line of progression, from utility operator to digester operator; TAPPI courses on kraft pulping.
tools: Chip bins, steaming vessels and chip meters
White liquor feed and heat exchangers

skills.name: Paper Machine Dry End Operation
skills.what: Running the dryer section, size press, calender and reel: setting steam pressures and draws, threading the tail after a break, and making the reel turn-up. A person who has it reads the quality control scanner's basis weight, moisture and caliper profiles, corrects them, and threads the sheet back through without a second break.
skills.learned: On the job as third hand and back tender.
tools: Rope and vacuum tail threading systems

skills.name: Paper Machine Wet End Operation
skills.what: Running the forming and press sections of a paper or board machine: the headbox, wire or twin-wire former, vacuum boxes and press felts. A person who has it sets the slice and the jet-to-wire ratio, reads drainage and formation, changes felts and wires on a shutdown, and brings the machine back up after a break.
skills.learned: On the job up the machine crew's line of progression, from fifth or fourth hand to machine tender; TAPPI's paper machine operator training and short courses.

skills.name: Pulp Bleaching
skills.what: Brightening pulp through an oxygen stage and a bleaching sequence of chlorine dioxide, caustic and peroxide. A person who has it sets the chemical charge, temperature and retention of each stage, holds brightness and residuals to target, and works safely around chlorine dioxide.
skills.learned: On the job in a bleach plant; TAPPI bleaching courses. Chlorine dioxide generation is trained and qualified unit by unit.

skills.name: Pulp Washing and Screening
skills.what: Separating cooked pulp from spent liquor and removing knots and shives by running knotters, pressure screens, cleaners and the brownstock washers (drum, diffusion or press). A person who has it balances dilution and wash water so soda loss and carryover stay low without weakening the liquor sent to recovery.
skills.learned: On the job in a pulp mill's fiber line.
tools: Rotary drum and pressure diffuser washers

skills.name: Pulp and Paper Testing
skills.what: Testing pulp, paper and board to TAPPI methods: kappa, freeness and brightness of pulp; basis weight, caliper, moisture, porosity and smoothness of paper; burst, ring crush, edge crush and Cobb of board and combined corrugated. A person who has it conditions and tests samples correctly, reads the results against the grade's specification, and tells the crew what to change.
skills.learned: On the job in a mill or box plant, to TAPPI test methods.
tools: Basis weight scales and caliper gauges
Burst, ring crush and edge crush testers

skills.name: Stock Preparation
skills.what: Making the furnish a paper machine runs on: repulping market pulp or recovered paper, cleaning and screening it, refining the fiber to freeness and blending it to consistency in the chests. A person who has it sets refiner load and flow, keeps cleaners and screens from plugging, and delivers stock at a steady consistency.
skills.learned: On the job in a paper mill, usually the first station of the machine crew's progression; TAPPI stock preparation courses.

skills.name: Paper Coating
