skills.what: Applying pigment coating to paper or board on a blade, rod, film or curtain coater and drying it. A person who has it sets coat weight and blade or rod pressure, controls coating viscosity and solids, and corrects streaks, scratches and blade bleeding.
skills.learned: On the job at a coated paper or board mill; TAPPI coating short courses.
tools: Blade, rod, film and curtain coaters

skills.name: Tissue Creping
skills.what: Drying a tissue sheet on a Yankee dryer and creping it off with a doctor blade to make it soft and bulky. A person who has it manages the Yankee coating chemistry, blade angle and blade changes, and the speed difference to the reel, and protects the Yankee's surface from damage.
skills.learned: On the job on a tissue machine; tissue courses from TAPPI and machine builders.

skills.name: Wet End Chemistry Control
skills.what: Keeping the chemistry of the wet end in balance: retention and drainage aids, sizing, starch, charge and pH, and the deposits and pitch they cause. A person who has it reads first-pass retention, charge and white-water consistency, traces a sheet defect or a runnability problem to its chemical cause, and corrects it with the chemical supplier.
skills.learned: Years on a machine, then supplier and TAPPI wet end chemistry courses; process engineers learn it in paper science degree programs.
tools: Charge analyzers and streaming current detectors

skills.name: Black Liquor Evaporation
skills.what: Concentrating weak black liquor in multiple-effect evaporators and concentrators so it can be burned in the recovery boiler. A person who has it holds solids and steam economy, boils out scaled effects, and keeps soap and condensates going where they belong.
skills.learned: On the job in a kraft mill's recovery area; TAPPI Kraft Recovery Operations Course.

skills.name: Recausticizing and Lime Kiln Operation
skills.what: Turning green liquor back into white liquor with lime, and reburning the lime mud in a rotary kiln. A person who has it controls slaker and causticizer conditions, clarifier and filter performance, and kiln firing, so the white liquor is strong and the lime reactive.
skills.learned: On the job in a kraft mill's recovery area; TAPPI Kraft Recovery Operations Course.
tools: White liquor and lime mud filters

skills.name: Recovery Boiler Operation
skills.what: Firing concentrated black liquor in a kraft recovery boiler to make steam and recover the smelt that holds the cooking chemicals. A person who has it controls liquor firing, air levels and the char bed, keeps the smelt spouts open, runs the sootblowers, and knows the emergency shutdown procedure for a water leak into the furnace, the boiler's worst hazard.
skills.learned: Years in the recovery area, the TAPPI Kraft Recovery Operations Course and the mill's qualification. The Black Liquor Recovery Boiler Advisory Committee publishes the safe firing and emergency shutdown practice mills follow; some states license boiler operators.

skills.name: Panel Layup and Mat Forming
skills.what: Building the panel before it is pressed: laying up veneer sheets with alternating grain for plywood or LVL, or forming oriented strand, particle or fiber mats to weight and orientation. A person who has it keeps the mat even, the layup in order and the weight right for the panel's grade.
skills.learned: On the job in a panel mill.

skills.name: Resin Blending
skills.what: Mixing and applying the adhesive a panel is bonded with: phenolic, urea or MDI resin and wax sprayed onto strands or particles in blenders, or glue mixed and spread for veneer. A person who has it holds resin and wax content to the recipe and handles isocyanate and formaldehyde resins safely.
skills.learned: On the job in a panel mill; resin suppliers train operators.

skills.name: Veneer Peeling
skills.what: Conditioning blocks and peeling them into veneer on a rotary lathe, then clipping the ribbon into sheets. A person who has it centers each block for the most veneer, sets the knife and nosebar gap for thickness, and keeps the knife sharp and the veneer smooth.
skills.learned: On the job in a plywood or LVL mill.

skills.name: Veneer and Furnish Drying
skills.what: Drying veneer in jet dryers, or strands, particles and fiber in rotary and tube dryers, to target moisture. A person who has it sets temperature and speed for species and thickness, grades or redries what comes out wet, and watches for fires.
skills.learned: On the job in a plywood, OSB, particleboard or MDF mill.

skills.name: Lumber Kiln Drying
skills.what: Drying lumber in steam or direct-fired kilns to a schedule: loading charges, setting dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures and venting, sampling moisture and stress, and conditioning at the end. A person who has it dries to target moisture without checks, warp, stain or collapse, and adjusts the schedule for species and thickness.
skills.learned: On the job at a sawmill; short courses on lumber drying given by university wood products programs.

skills.name: Panel Hot Pressing
skills.what: Running the hot press that cures a panel, setting the temperature, pressure and time profile of a platen or continuous press. A person who has it reads the press curve and the board's density profile, prevents blows and delamination, and changes the cycle for each product.
skills.learned: Years in a panel mill, at the press after the stations before it.

skills.name: Ceramic Kiln Firing
skills.what: Firing brick, tile, sanitaryware, refractories and technical ceramics in tunnel, roller and periodic kilns: setting the kiln cars or loads, running the firing curve through heat-up, soak and cooling, and checking the fired ware for size, color and cracks. A person who has it holds the curve the ware needs, and finds which zone made a defect.
skills.learned: On the job in a brick or ceramics plant.

skills.name: Grinding Mill Operation
skills.what: Running the mills that grind raw meal, coal, clinker, lime or gypsum: setting feed, table pressure or charge, separator speed and air flow, and holding the product's fineness and moisture. A person who has it reads mill power, sound and pressure drop, and keeps a mill from choking or running empty.
skills.learned: On the job in a cement or mineral plant, often from the control room.
tools: Ball mills and vertical roller mills

skills.name: Rotary Kiln Operation
skills.what: Running a cement or lime kiln system so clinker or lime comes out at the quality wanted: raw meal feed, preheater and calciner, fuel and flame, kiln speed, cooler and draft. A person who has it reads burning zone temperature, shell scanner, gas analysis and free lime together, keeps the coating stable, and brings the kiln through an upset without damage.
skills.learned: Years as a plant operator, then training on the kiln beside a qualified burner. Online courses in kiln pyroprocessing are widely used.
tools: Preheater towers, calciners and rotary kilns

skills.name: Test Equipment Design
skills.what: Designing the stand, station, rack or fixture a product is tested on: the instruments and switching, the connection to the unit under test, the wiring, the interlocks, and the proof that the equipment itself is right before it is used. A person who has it turns a test requirement into equipment a technician can run, with its drawings and its own acceptance test.
skills.learned: On the job as a test engineer, from an electrical or mechanical engineering degree. No credential.

skills.name: Serial Bus Diagnostics
skills.what: Checking the serial links between chips, boards and units: I2C and SPI on a board, UART, RS-232, RS-422 and RS-485 between units. A person who has it sets up the port, reads the traffic with a logic or protocol analyzer and finds a wiring, addressing, termination or timing fault.
skills.learned: Electronics programs at community colleges and electrical engineering study; on the job at a test bench.

skills.name: Environmental Chamber Testing
skills.what: Running a product through a temperature, humidity or altitude profile in a chamber to prove it works across the conditions it is rated for. A person who has it loads and instruments the unit, programs the profile, and watches the unit through each dwell and transition for drift or failure.
skills.learned: On the job in a test laboratory, working to the test methods the product is qualified to (MIL-STD-810 and RTCA DO-160 in aerospace and defence).

skills.name: Sewing Machine Repair
skills.what: Keeping industrial sewing machines sewing: timing the hook or looper to the needle, setting needle bar height, feed, presser foot and tension, replacing worn parts and servo motors, and setting up attachments and automatic units for a new operation. A person who has it finds why a machine skips, breaks thread or puckers and fixes it at the operator's station.
skills.learned: On the job as a sewing machine mechanic, often after time as an operator; machine dealers run mechanics' courses.

skills.name: Knitting Machine Setup and Repair
skills.what: Setting up and repairing knitting machines: changing style, gauge and pattern, setting cams, stitch length and yarn feed, replacing needles, sinkers and cylinders, and tracing a recurring defect to its part. A person who has it changes a machine to a new style and has it knitting first quality on the first roll.
skills.learned: On the job as a knitting fixer; machine makers train technicians.

skills.name: Loom Setup and Repair
skills.what: Setting up, timing and repairing weaving machines: style changes, harness and reed changes, shed, pick and let-off settings, and finding why a loom keeps stopping or marking the cloth. A person who has it fixes a set of looms through a shift and overhauls one back to its timing chart.
skills.learned: On the job as a loom fixer, usually after years as a weaver; loom makers run courses for technicians.

skills.name: Spinning Machine Setup and Repair
skills.what: Setting and repairing the machines of a yarn mill: card clothing and flat settings, drafting zones, spindles, rings and travelers, rotors and winding heads, and changing a frame over to a new count. A person who has it brings a machine back to standard after a fault or an overhaul and proves it on the yarn.
skills.learned: On the job as a card or spinning fixer, after time as an operator; machine makers train fixers on their equipment.
tools: Card clothing mounting and grinding equipment

skills.name: Tufting Machine Setup and Repair
skills.what: Setting up and repairing tufting machines: style set-up, needle bar and gauge parts, reblading and rehooking, setting loopers, knives and backing feed, and the pattern attachments. A person who has it changes a machine over to a new style and finds why it is streaking or skipping.
skills.learned: On the job as a tufting fixer or mechanic, after time as an operator; machine makers train mechanics.

skills.name: Branch Circuit Wiring
skills.what: Wiring 120- and 240-volt AC circuits: the panelboard, branch circuits to receptacles, lights and appliances, ground-fault and arc-fault protection, and the shore power or utility inlet. A person who has it wires to the electrical code, keeps polarity and grounding right and proves each circuit before it is energized.
skills.learned: Electrical apprenticeships and programs; on the job at RV, boat and modular building plants, which wire to the National Electrical Code (RVs to its Article 551) and boats to ABYC E-11.

skills.name: Ammonia Refrigeration System Operation
skills.what: Running and servicing an industrial ammonia refrigeration plant: starting, loading and stopping screw and reciprocating compressors from their panels; watching suction and discharge pressures, condensers, vessels and defrost; draining oil and purging air; isolating and pumping down equipment for work; and keeping the logs and procedures the process safety rules require. A person who has it holds the rooms and the process at temperature and responds correctly to an ammonia leak.
skills.learned: On the job under a senior operator; the Refrigerating Engineers and Technicians Association's CARO, CIRO and CRST certifications; IIAR training. A plant with more than 10,000 pounds of ammonia falls under OSHA's process safety management standard.

skills.name: Building Automation System Operation
skills.what: Running a building's heating, cooling, ventilation and utility plant from its automation system: reading the graphics, trends and alarms, changing setpoints and schedules, and finding whether a complaint is the sensor, the controller or the equipment. A person who has it answers an alarm from the workstation first, trends a point before changing it, and leaves an override with a note and an end date.
skills.learned: On the job on the site's system; the control makers and their dealers teach operator and technician courses.

skills.name: Railcar Air Brake Testing
skills.what: Testing a freight car's air brake system with a single car test device to the code of the Association of American Railroads: charging, leakage, application and release, service and emergency, retainer and piston travel, then recording the test on the car. A person who has it finds a failed valve or a leak and replaces the part before the retest.
skills.learned: On the job at a railcar shop, with the employer's qualification to the AAR's single car test; the federal freight brake rules (49 CFR Part 232) govern the work.

skills.name: Railcar Truck Assembly
skills.what: Building and repairing the trucks a railcar rides on: setting side frames, bolster, springs and friction wedges, mounting wheelsets with their roller bearing adapters, and gauging wear against the limits of the AAR's interchange rules. A person who has it jacks and blocks a car safely to change a wheelset.
skills.learned: On the job at a railcar builder or repair shop.

skills.name: Coupler and Draft Gear Service
skills.what: Removing, inspecting and fitting couplers, knuckles, yokes and draft gear: gauging contour and knuckle wear, applying the right pins, keys and retainers, and setting coupler height. A person who has it knows the condemning limits the interchange rules give.
skills.learned: On the job at a railcar builder or repair shop.
tools: Draft gear jacks and lifting tools

skills.name: Fabric Inspection
skills.what: Inspecting greige or finished fabric for defects on an inspection frame by a points system: marking and grading each defect, measuring width and length, and deciding whether a roll ships, is cut around or goes to seconds. A person who has it knows the common weaving, knitting and dyeing defects by sight and grades a roll the way another inspector would.
skills.learned: On the job in a mill, or at a cut-and-sew plant's receiving. The four-point system is written in ASTM D5430.
tools: Fabric inspection frames and light tables

skills.name: Wood Moisture Content Measurement
skills.what: Measuring how much water is in wood, with pin and pinless meters and by oven-dry samples, correcting for species and temperature. A person who has it samples a package or kiln charge properly, and knows whether lumber is dry enough to grade, ship or machine.
skills.learned: On the job; covered in kiln drying and lumber grading courses.

skills.name: Hardwood Lumber Grading
skills.what: Grading hardwood lumber to the National Hardwood Lumber Association's rules: measuring each board's surface measure and working out the clear cuttings it yields. A person who has it tallies and grades boards fast and accurately enough for lumber to be bought and sold on the grade.
skills.learned: The National Hardwood Lumber Association's Inspector Training School (eight weeks in Memphis, or a hybrid course) and its short courses; on the job.

skills.name: Softwood Lumber Grading
skills.what: Grading softwood lumber and timbers by eye to an agency's grading rules: reading knots, wane, splits, slope of grain and warp on every face, and marking the grade or trimming to a better one. A person who has it grades at the speed of the line, and stays within the agency's tolerance when checked.
skills.learned: Grader training at the mill, then certification and regular checks by a grading agency accredited by the American Lumber Standard Committee, such as WWPA, SPIB or NeLMA.

skills.name: Automated Lumber Grading
skills.what: Running and tuning an automatic grading system that scans each board and assigns its grade and trim: checking its decisions against the rules, adjusting defect and grade settings, and auditing samples with the grading agency. A person who has it keeps the machine grading on rule and on value.
skills.learned: On the job, after experience as a certified grader; scanner makers train their users.

skills.name: Advanced Product Quality Planning
skills.what: Planning a new part's quality from concept to launch in set phases, so that the design and process risks, the control plan, the measurement studies and the part approval are done before production starts. A person who has it can run the plan for a part or a supplier and knows what each phase must deliver.
skills.learned: Employer and customer training in automotive and aerospace supply chains; AIAG's APQP manual is the reference. Covered by ASQ's Certified Quality Engineer.

removed.why: Aircraft line maintenance, flight-line servicing and avionics function checks. These are tasks from an aircraft's maintenance manual rather than skills a plant hires for, and no career used them.
A material, fluid or product name. Working with a material is part of the process skill that uses it.
A specification, regulation or accreditation scheme, not something a person does. The process each one governs is kept as a skill and names the standard where it matters.

Installing or building one named product or system: a weapon, sensor, avionics unit, airframe section or motor variant. Too narrow to be a skill of its own; the fastening, wiring, sealing and rigging skills cover the work, and no career used these.
Knowledge of, or work on, one company's named product. Each was on one or two career paths; those paths keep the transferable skills beside it.
Launch, flight and mission operations: not manufacturing work.
Theory, background knowledge or a topic too vague to be shown or assessed.
Supervision, planning, clerical and warehouse work, and general awareness topics. The catalogue is for technical skills of the plant floor and its engineering office.
Design, analysis and reference software, and CAD techniques, that no career used. The CAD and CAM packages careers do use are kept.
A real method or process, but on no career, and no career in the catalogue plainly needs it.
